title.zh: 卷一百六十七 列傳第五十四: 張立道 張庭珍 張惠 劉好禮 王國昌 姜彧 張礎 呂掞𡌳 譚資榮 王惲
title.en: Volume 167 Biographies 54: Zhang Lidao, Zhang Tingzhen, Zhang Hui, Liu Haoli, Wang Guochang, Jiang Yu, Zhang Chu, Lu Shan, Tan Zirong, Wang Yun
title.raw: 卷一百六十七 列傳第五十四: 張立道 張庭珍 張惠 劉好禮 王國昌 姜彧 張礎 呂掞𡌳 譚資榮 王惲 Volume 167 Biographies 54: Zhang Lidao, Zhang Tingzhen, Zhang Hui, Liu Haoli, Wang Guochang, Jiang Yu, Zhang Chu, Lu Shan, Tan Zirong, Wang Yun

sentences.zh: 張立道

translations.literal: Zhang Lidao
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Lidao

sentences.zh: 張立道，字顯卿。

translations.literal: Zhang Lidao, courtesy name Xianqing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Lidao, whose courtesy name was Xianqing.

sentences.zh: 其先陳留人，後徙大名。

translations.literal: His ancestors were men of Chenliu; later they moved to Daming.
translations.idiomatic: His family originally came from Chenliu and later relocated to Daming.

sentences.zh: 父善，登金進土第。

translations.literal: His father Shan passed the Jin jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shan had passed the Jin dynasty jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 歲壬辰，國兵下河南，善以策幹太第拖雷，命為必阇赤。

translations.literal: In the year renchen, the state army descended on Henan; Shan presented his plans to Imperial Younger Brother Tolui and was appointed a bituxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the renchen year, when the imperial armies swept into Henan, Shan offered his counsel to Prince Tolui and was appointed a bituxi.

sentences.zh: 立道年十七，以父任備宿衛。

translations.literal: Lidao at age seventeen, through his father's position, served in the palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: At seventeen, Lidao entered palace service on his father's recommendation.

sentences.zh: 世祖即位，立道從北征，未嘗去左右。

translations.literal: When the Founder took the throne, Lidao followed the northern campaign and never left his side.
translations.idiomatic: After Kublai's accession, Lidao accompanied the northern campaign and never left his side.

sentences.zh: 至元四年，命立道使西夏，給所部軍儲，以乾敏稱。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhiyuan, Lidao was ordered to go to Xixia to supply army provisions to the troops under his charge; he was known for capability and quickness.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiyuan 4 he was sent to Xixia to provision the troops under his command and won a reputation for efficiency and resourcefulness.

sentences.zh: 皇子忽哥赤封雲南王，往鎮其地，詔以立道為王府文學。

translations.literal: The prince Huguqi was enfeoffed as Prince of Yunnan and went to govern that region; an edict appointed Lidao literary officer of the princely establishment.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Huguqi was enfeoffed as Prince of Yunnan and went to take up his post, Lidao was appointed literary officer of the princely household.

sentences.zh: 立道勸王務農以厚民，即署立道大理等處勸農官，兼領屯田事，佩銀符。

translations.literal: Lidao urged the prince to devote himself to agriculture to enrich the people; he was immediately appointed agriculture-promotion officer for Dali and other places, concurrently in charge of garrison farming, and wore a silver tally.
translations.idiomatic: Lidao urged the prince to promote farming to enrich the people. He was then appointed agriculture officer for Dali and neighboring districts, put in charge of garrison farming as well, and given a silver tally.

sentences.zh: 尋與侍郎寧端甫使安南，定歲貢之禮。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he went with Vice Minister Ning Duanfu as envoy to Annam and fixed the annual tribute protocol.
translations.idiomatic: He soon went with Vice Minister Ning Duanfu to Annam as envoy and established the rules for the annual tribute.

sentences.zh: 雲南三十七部都元帥寶合丁專制歲久，有竊據之志，忌忽哥赤來為王，設宴置毒酒中，且賂王相府官無洩其事。

translations.literal: Boheding, commander-in-chief of Yunnan's thirty-seven divisions, had held sole power for many years and harbored designs of usurpation; he resented Huguqi's coming as prince, set poison in wine at a banquet, and bribed officials of the princely chancellery not to reveal the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Boheding, the commander-in-chief of Yunnan's thirty-seven divisions, had ruled alone for years and coveted power for himself. He resented Huguqi's arrival as prince, poisoned the wine at a banquet, and bribed the prince's chancellery officials to keep quiet.

sentences.zh: 立道聞之，趨入見，守門者拒之，立道怒與爭。

translations.literal: Lidao heard of it and hurried in to see the prince; the gatekeepers barred him, and Lidao angrily argued with them.
translations.idiomatic: When Lidao heard of it he rushed in to warn the prince, but the gatekeepers turned him away and he argued with them in anger.

sentences.zh: 王聞其聲，使人召立道，乃得入，為王言之。

translations.literal: The prince heard his voice and sent someone to summon Lidao; only then could he enter and tell the prince.
translations.idiomatic: The prince heard the commotion and sent for him. Lidao was admitted and told the prince what was happening.

sentences.zh: 王引其手，使探口中，肉已腐矣。

translations.literal: The prince drew his hand and had him feel inside his mouth; the flesh was already rotting.
translations.idiomatic: The prince took his hand and had him feel inside his mouth—the flesh was already rotting.

sentences.zh: 是夕，王薨。

translations.literal: That evening the prince died.
translations.idiomatic: That night the prince died.

sentences.zh: 寶合丁遂據王座，使人諷王妃索王印。

translations.literal: Boheding then seized the prince's seat and sent someone to hint to the princess that she should surrender the princely seal.
translations.idiomatic: Boheding then took the prince's seat and sent someone to press the princess consort for the princely seal.

sentences.zh: 立道潛結義士，得十三人，約共討賊，刺臂血和金屑飲之，推一人走京師告變。

translations.literal: Lidao secretly rallied men of honor and gathered thirteen; they pledged to join in punishing the traitor, pricked their arms and mixed the blood with gold dust to drink it, and chose one man to hurry to the capital to report the emergency.
translations.idiomatic: Lidao secretly gathered thirteen loyal men, swore an oath to punish the traitor by mixing arm-blood with gold dust and drinking it together, and sent one of them to the capital to report the crisis.

sentences.zh: 事頗露，寶合丁乃囚立道，將殺之。

translations.literal: The affair leaked out somewhat; Boheding then imprisoned Lidao and was about to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: When the plot began to leak out, Boheding imprisoned Lidao and prepared to execute him.

sentences.zh: 人匠提舉張忠者，燕人也，於立道為族兄，結壯士夜劫諸獄，出之，共亡至土蕃界，遇帝所遣御史大夫博羅歡、王傅別怗與告變人俱來。

translations.literal: Zhang Zhong, superintendent of artisans, a man of Yan and Lidao's clansman elder brother, gathered stalwarts and by night raided the prisons to free him; together they fled to the Tibetan frontier, where they met the Grand Censor Boluohuan and the prince's tutor Biezhe, whom the emperor had sent, together with the man who had reported the emergency.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhong of Yan, superintendent of artisans and Lidao's elder clansman, rallied strong men and raided the prisons by night to free him. They fled together to the Tibetan frontier, where they met Grand Censor Boluohuan and Prince's Tutor Biezhe, sent by the emperor, along with the man who had reported the crisis.

sentences.zh: 二人者遂與立道俱還，按寶合丁及王府官嘗受賂者，皆伏誅。

translations.literal: The two men then returned with Lidao, investigated Boheding and the princely-house officials who had accepted bribes, and all were executed.
translations.idiomatic: The two officials returned with Lidao, tried Boheding and the bribed princely-house officials, and had them all executed.

sentences.zh: 有旨召立道等入朝，問王薨時狀。

translations.literal: An edict summoned Lidao and the others to court and asked about the circumstances of the prince's death.
translations.idiomatic: An edict summoned Lidao and his companions to court to report on the prince's death.

sentences.zh: 帝聞立道言，泣數行下，歔欷久之，曰：「汝等為我家事甚勞苦，今欲事朕乎，事太子乎，事安西王乎？

translations.literal: When the emperor heard Lidao's account, tears ran down his face for several lines; he sighed long and said: "You have toiled greatly for my family's affairs. Do you now wish to serve Me, serve the Crown Prince, or serve the Prince of Anxi?"
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard Lidao's account, tears streamed down his face and he sighed for a long while. "You have borne great hardship for my house," he said. "Will you serve me, the crown prince, or the Prince of Anxi?"

sentences.zh: 惟妝意所向。

translations.literal: Follow only where your hearts incline.
translations.idiomatic: Go wherever your hearts lead you.

sentences.zh: 」立道等奏願留事陛下，於是賜立道金五十兩，以​​旌其忠，張忠等亦皆授官有差。

translations.literal: Lidao and the others memorialized that they wished to remain in the emperor's service; thereupon Lidao was granted fifty taels of gold to honor his loyalty, and Zhang Zhong and the others were also given offices of varying rank.
translations.idiomatic: Lidao and the others asked to remain in the emperor's service. The emperor then gave Lidao fifty taels of gold to honor his loyalty, and Zhang Zhong and the others received appointments of varying rank.

sentences.zh: 八年，復使安南，宣建國號詔。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was again sent to Annam to proclaim the edict establishing the dynastic title.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was again sent to Annam to proclaim the edict establishing the dynastic name.

sentences.zh: 立道並黑水，跨雲南，以至其國，歲貢之禮遂定。

translations.literal: Lidao traversed Heishui, crossed Yunnan, and reached that country; the annual tribute protocol was thereby settled.
translations.idiomatic: Lidao traveled through Heishui and across Yunnan to reach Annam, and the annual tribute arrangements were settled.

sentences.zh: 十年三月，領大司農事，中書以立道熟於雲南，奏授大理等處巡行勸農使，佩金符。

translations.literal: In the third month of the tenth year he took charge of the Grand Secretariat of Agriculture; the Central Secretariat, because Lidao was well acquainted with Yunnan, memorialized to appoint him touring agriculture-promotion commissioner for Dali and other places, with a gold tally.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the tenth year he took charge of the Grand Secretariat of Agriculture. Because he knew Yunnan well, the Central Secretariat had him appointed touring agriculture commissioner for Dali and neighboring districts, with a gold tally.

sentences.zh: 其地有昆明池，介碧雞、金馬之間，環五百餘里，夏潦暴至，必冒城郭。

translations.literal: In that region is Lake Kunming, lying between Biji and Jinma, encircling more than five hundred li; in summer sudden floods would invariably inundate the walled towns.
translations.idiomatic: The region had Lake Kunming, lying between Biji and Jinma and spanning more than five hundred li. Every summer sudden floods would swamp the walled towns.

sentences.zh: 立道求泉源所自出，役丁夫二千人治之，洩其水，得壞地萬餘頃，皆為良田。

translations.literal: Lidao sought the source of the springs, employed two thousand laborers to manage them, drained off the water, and gained more than ten thousand qing of ruined land, all turned into fertile fields.
translations.idiomatic: Lidao traced the springs to their source, put two thousand laborers to work on them, and drained the water off. More than ten thousand qing of flooded land became fertile fields.

sentences.zh: 爨、僰之人雖知蠶桑，而未得其法，立道始教之飼養，收利十倍於舊，雲南之人由是益富庶。

translations.literal: The Cuan and Bo people, though knowing silkworms and mulberry, had not mastered the methods; Lidao first taught them rearing and feeding, and the harvest profit was ten times the old amount; the people of Yunnan thereby grew still more prosperous.
translations.idiomatic: The Cuan and Bo peoples knew sericulture in a rough way but not the proper methods. Lidao taught them how to raise silkworms, and yields rose tenfold. Yunnan grew noticeably wealthier as a result.

sentences.zh: 羅羅諸山蠻慕之，相率來降，收其地悉為郡縣。

translations.literal: The Luoluo and various mountain tribes admired this and came in succession to submit; their lands were all taken in and made into prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Luoluo and other mountain tribes admired his work and submitted in groups. Their territories were organized into prefectures and counties.

sentences.zh: 十五年，除中慶路總管，佩虎符。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was appointed director-general of Zhongqing Route and wore a tiger tally.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he was made director-general of Zhongqing Route and given a tiger tally.

sentences.zh: 先是雲南未知尊孔子，祀王逸少為先師。

translations.literal: Previously Yunnan did not yet know to honor Confucius and sacrificed to Wang Yishao as the founding teacher.
translations.idiomatic: Until then Yunnan had not honored Confucius and instead venerated Wang Xizhi as the founding teacher.

sentences.zh: 立道首建孔子廟，置學舍，勸士人子弟以學，擇蜀士之賢者，迎以為弟子師，歲時率諸生行釋菜禮，人習禮讓，風俗稍變矣。

translations.literal: Lidao was the first to build a Confucius temple, establish schoolhouses, and urge the sons of scholar-gentry to study; he selected worthy men from Shu and welcomed them as teachers of the disciples; at the seasons he led the students in the libation-of-vegetables rite; people practiced courtesy and deference, and customs gradually changed.
translations.idiomatic: Lidao built the first Confucius temple, set up schools, and urged gentry sons to study. He brought worthy scholars from Shu to serve as teachers, led the students in seasonal libation rites, and gradually changed local customs toward courtesy and decorum.

sentences.zh: 行省平章賽典赤表言於朝，有旨進官以褒之。

translations.literal: Sayid Ajall, regional secretary grand councillor, memorialized the court; an edict ordered his promotion to commend him.
translations.idiomatic: Regional Secretary Sayid Ajall memorialized the court on his behalf, and an edict promoted him in recognition of his service.

sentences.zh: 十七年，入朝，力請於帝以雲南王子也先帖木兒襲王爵，帝從之。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he entered court and strongly petitioned the emperor that the Yunnan prince's son Yesün Temür should inherit the princely title; the emperor assented.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he went to court and strongly urged that the Yunnan prince's son Yesün Temür inherit the title. The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 遂命立道為臨安廣西道宣撫使，兼管軍招討使，仍佩虎符，陛辭，賜以弓矢、衣服、鞍馬。

translations.literal: He was then appointed pacification commissioner of Lin'an and Guangxi Circuit, concurrently commander of the army for punitive campaigns, still wearing a tiger tally; on farewell at the throne he was granted bows and arrows, robes, and saddle horses.
translations.idiomatic: Lidao was then appointed pacification commissioner of Lin'an-Guangxi Circuit and commander of punitive forces, again with a tiger tally. At his farewell audience the emperor gave him bows, arrows, robes, and horses.

sentences.zh: 始赴任，會禾泥路大首領必思反，扇動諸蠻夷。

translations.literal: Just as he was setting out to take up his post, the great chief Bisi of Hemi Route rebelled and incited the various tribal peoples.
translations.idiomatic: As he was setting out for his post, the great chief Bisi of Hemi Route rebelled and stirred up the tribal peoples.

sentences.zh: 及發兵討之，拔其城邑，鼓行而前，徇金齒甸七十城，越麻甸，抵可蒲，皆下之。

translations.literal: When he sent troops to punish them, he captured their walled towns, advanced with drums beating, swept through seventy cities of Jinchi district, crossed Madian, and reached Kebu—all were taken.
translations.idiomatic: He marched against them, took their walled towns, and advanced with drums beating. He subdued seventy cities in Jinchi district, crossed Madian, reached Kebu, and took them all.

sentences.zh: 有遺以馴象、金鳳異物者，悉獻諸朝。

translations.literal: When people presented tame elephants, golden phoenixes, and other rare objects, he sent them all as tribute to the court.
translations.idiomatic: Tame elephants, golden phoenixes, and other rare gifts he received were all sent to court as tribute.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，又籍兩江儂士貴、岑從毅、李維屏所部戶二十五萬有奇，以其籍歸有司。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he again registered the households under Nong Shigui, Cen Congyi, and Li Weiping of the Two Rivers—more than two hundred fifty thousand odd—and returned their registers to the regular officials.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year he registered more than 250,000 households under Nong Shigui, Cen Congyi, and Li Weiping of the Two Rivers and turned the registers over to the civil authorities.

sentences.zh: 遷臨安廣西道軍民​​宣撫使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be pacification commissioner for the military and civilian population of Lin'an and Guangxi Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to pacification commissioner for military and civilian affairs in Lin'an-Guangxi Circuit.

sentences.zh: 复創廟學於建水路，書清白之訓於公廨，以警貪墨，風化大行。

translations.literal: He again founded temple schools on Jianshui Route, wrote admonitions on integrity in the government offices to warn against corruption, and moral transformation was greatly carried out.
translations.idiomatic: He founded more temple schools on Jianshui Route and posted admonitions on integrity in government offices to warn against corruption. Public morals improved markedly.

sentences.zh: 入朝，值權臣用事，遂退居散地。

translations.literal: On entering court, he encountered a time when powerful ministers held sway, and so he withdrew to an honorary post.
translations.idiomatic: When he went to court, powerful ministers were in control, so he withdrew to an honorary post.

sentences.zh: 條陳十二策，皆切當之務，帝嘉納焉。

translations.literal: He submitted twelve policy items in detail, all pressing affairs; the emperor praised and adopted them.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted twelve policy proposals on urgent matters, and the emperor praised and adopted them.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，北京地陷，人民震驚，命立道為本路總管。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year the ground in Dadu collapsed and the people were alarmed; Lidao was ordered to be director-general of that route.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year the ground in Dadu collapsed and frightened the populace. Lidao was appointed director-general of the route.

sentences.zh: 未行，安南世子陳日燇遣其臣嚴仲維、陳子良等詣京師告襲爵。

translations.literal: Before he could depart, the Annamese heir Chen Rizhuan sent his ministers Yan Zhongwei, Chen Ziliang, and others to the capital to report succession to the title.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could take up the post, the Annamese heir Chen Rizhuan sent ministers Yan Zhongwei and Chen Ziliang to court to announce his succession.

sentences.zh: 先是，其國主陳日烜累召不至，權遣其族父遺愛入貢，朝廷因封為安南王。

translations.literal: Earlier, the ruler Chen Rixuan had been summoned repeatedly but did not come; he had his clansman uncle Yi'ai go in to offer tribute, and the court thereupon enfeoffed Yi'ai as King of Annam.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the ruler Chen Rixuan had ignored repeated summonses to court. He sent his clansman Yi'ai to offer tribute instead, and the court enfeoffed Yi'ai as King of Annam.

sentences.zh: 遺愛還，日烜陰害之。

translations.literal: When Yi'ai returned, Rixuan secretly harmed him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yi'ai returned, Rixuan had him killed in secret.

sentences.zh: 遣使問罪，日烜拒使者不受命，遂遣將討之，失利而還。

translations.literal: An envoy was sent to demand an accounting; Rixuan refused the envoy and would not accept orders; generals were then sent to punish him, but they returned after meeting defeat.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent an envoy to demand an accounting, but Rixuan refused to obey. A punitive force was sent and returned in defeat.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，欲再發兵，丞相完澤、平章不忽木言：「蠻夷小邦，不足以勞中國。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and wished to send troops again; Chancellor Wanze and Grand Councillor Buqum said: "A petty barbarian state is not worth troubling the Middle Kingdom."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and wanted to send troops again. Chancellor Wanze and Grand Councillor Buqum said, "A petty frontier state is not worth mobilizing the empire for."

sentences.zh: 張立道嘗再使安南有功，今復使往，宜無不奉命。

translations.literal: Zhang Lidao has twice been envoy to Annam with merit; if he is sent again, they surely will not fail to obey."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Lidao has been to Annam twice with success. Send him again and they will surely obey."

sentences.zh: 」帝招至香殿，諭之曰：「小國不恭，今遣汝往諭朕意，宜盡乃心。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned him to the Fragrant Hall and instructed him: "The small state has been disrespectful; I now send you to convey My intent—you should devote your whole heart."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned him to the Fragrant Hall and said, "That small state has been disrespectful. I am sending you to convey my will. Give the mission your full devotion."

sentences.zh: 」立道對曰：「君父之命，雖蹈水火不敢辭，臣愚恐不足專任，乞重臣一人與俱，臣為之副。

translations.literal: Lidao replied: "A lord-and-father's command—even treading fire or water one dare not refuse. This subject is foolish and fears he is not sufficient to bear sole responsibility; I beg one weighty minister to go together, with me as his deputy."
translations.idiomatic: Lidao replied, "A command from my sovereign is not to be refused even at the cost of my life. But I fear I am not equal to the task alone. I beg that a senior minister go with me while I serve as his deputy."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「卿朕腹心臣，使一人居卿上，必敗卿謀。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "You are My trusted inner minister; if I place someone above you, he will surely ruin your plan."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "You are my trusted inner minister. If I put someone over you, he will ruin your plan."

sentences.zh: 」遂授禮部尚書，佩三珠虎符，賜衣段、金鞍、弓矢以行。

translations.literal: He was then appointed Minister of Rites, wore a three-pearl tiger tally, and was granted silks, a gold saddle, and bow and arrows for the journey.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Minister of Rites, given a three-pearl tiger tally, and sent off with silks, a gold saddle, bow, and arrows.

sentences.zh: 至安南界，謂郊勞者曰：「語爾​​世子，當出郭迎詔。

translations.literal: On reaching the Annam border he told those who came to greet him at the suburbs: "Tell your heir that he should come outside the walls to welcome the edict."
translations.idiomatic: At the Annam border he told the welcoming party, "Tell your heir he must come outside the walls to receive the imperial edict."

sentences.zh: 」日燇乃率其屬，焚香伏謁道左。

translations.literal: Rizhuan then led his followers, burned incense, and prostrated themselves in obeisance by the roadside.
translations.idiomatic: Rizhuan then led his followers out, burned incense, and prostrated themselves by the roadside.

sentences.zh: 既抵府，日燇拜跪，聽詔如禮。

translations.literal: When they reached the prefectural seat, Rizhuan bowed and knelt and heard the edict according to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: At the capital Rizhuan bowed and knelt and received the edict with full ceremony.

sentences.zh: 立道傳上命，數其罪，為書曉之。

translations.literal: Lidao conveyed the emperor's command, enumerated their crimes, and wrote a letter to enlighten them.
translations.idiomatic: Lidao conveyed the imperial command, listed their offenses, and wrote a letter explaining the court's position.

sentences.zh: 日燇曰：「比三世辱公使，公大國之卿，小國之師也，何以教我？

translations.literal: Rizhuan said: "For three generations we have disgraced your envoys. You are a minister of a great state and the teacher of a small state—what could you teach me?"
translations.idiomatic: Rizhuan said, "For three generations we have mistreated your envoys. You are a minister of a great power and the teacher of a small one—what can you teach me?"

sentences.zh: 」立道曰：「昔鎮南王奉詞致討，汝非能勝之也，由其不用嚮導，率眾深入，不見一人，遲疑而還​​，曾未出險，風雨驟至，弓矢盡壞，眾不戰而自潰，天子亦既知之。

translations.literal: Lidao said: "Formerly the Prince of Zhennan came with an edict to punish you—you were not able to defeat him. It was because he did not use guides, led his host deep in, saw not a single man, hesitated and returned; he had not yet left the danger when wind and rain came suddenly, bows and arrows were all ruined, and the host collapsed without fighting—the Son of Heaven already knows this."
translations.idiomatic: Lidao said, "When the Prince of Zhennan came to punish you, you did not defeat him. He marched deep without guides, saw no enemy, hesitated, and turned back. Before he had even cleared the danger zone, wind and rain struck, his bows and arrows failed, and his army collapsed without a fight. The Son of Heaven knows this already."

sentences.zh: 汝所恃者，山海之險、瘴癘之惡耳。

translations.literal: What you rely on is only the peril of mountains and seas and the malignity of miasma—that is all.
translations.idiomatic: All you rely on are mountain barriers, sea routes, and malarial country—that is all.

sentences.zh: 且雲南與嶺南之人，習俗同，技力等，今發而用之，繼以北方之勁卒，汝復能抗哉？

translations.literal: Moreover, the people of Yunnan and Lingnan share the same customs and equal fighting strength; if they are now mobilized and used, followed by the hardy troops of the north—can you again resist?
translations.idiomatic: The peoples of Yunnan and Lingnan share your customs and match your fighting strength. Deploy them now, follow with northern veterans—could you still resist?

sentences.zh: 汝戰不利，不過遁入海中，島夷乘釁，必來寇抄汝，汝食少不能支，必為彼屈，汝為其臣，孰若為天子臣乎？

translations.literal: If you fight and fare ill, you can only flee into the sea; island barbarians will seize the opportunity and surely come to raid and plunder you; with little food you cannot sustain yourselves and will surely submit to them—is it not better to be the Son of Heaven's subject than theirs?
translations.idiomatic: If you lose, you can only flee to the sea. Island peoples will seize the chance to raid you. With little food you cannot hold out and will submit to them. Is it not better to be the Son of Heaven's subject than theirs?

sentences.zh: 今海上諸夷，歲貢於汝者，亦畏我大國之爾與也。

translations.literal: Now the various island peoples who pay you annual tribute also fear the awe of Our great state.
translations.idiomatic: Even the island peoples who pay you annual tribute fear the power of our great state.

sentences.zh: 聖天子有德於汝甚厚。

translations.literal: The sage Son of Heaven has shown you very great virtue.
translations.idiomatic: The sage Son of Heaven has shown you great forbearance.

sentences.zh: 前年之師，殊非上意，邊將讒汝爾。

translations.literal: The campaign of the year before last was wholly not the court's intent; frontier generals slandered you—that is all.
translations.idiomatic: The campaign two years ago was not the court's true intent. Frontier generals slandered you—that is all.

sentences.zh: 汝曾不悟，不能遣一介之使，謝罪請命，輒稱兵抗拒，逐我使人，以怒我大國之師，今禍且至矣，惟世子計之。

translations.literal: You never understood, could not send a single envoy to confess guilt and beg orders, but rashly raised arms in resistance and drove away Our envoys to anger the armies of Our great state—disaster is now about to arrive; let the heir alone consider it."
translations.idiomatic: You never understood. You sent no envoy to confess guilt and beg mercy, but raised arms, drove away our envoys, and provoked the armies of our great state. Disaster is near. Let the heir consider that."

sentences.zh: 」日燇拜，且泣涕而言曰​​：「公之言良是也，為我計者，皆不知出此。

translations.literal: Rizhuan bowed and, weeping, said: "Your words are indeed right; those who plan for me all did not know to come forth with this."
translations.idiomatic: Rizhuan bowed and said through tears, "You speak the truth. None of my advisers ever told me this."

sentences.zh: 前日之戰，救死而已，寧不知懼！

translations.literal: The battle of the other day was only to save our lives—how could we not fear!
translations.idiomatic: We fought the other day only to save our lives. Of course we were afraid!

sentences.zh: 天子使公來，必能活我。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven sent you—surely you can spare my life.
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven sent you—you can surely spare my life.

sentences.zh: 」北面再拜，誓死不敢忘天子之德。

translations.literal: Facing north he bowed twice and swore that until death he would not dare forget the Son of Heaven's virtue."
translations.idiomatic: He bowed toward the north twice and swore never to forget the Son of Heaven's grace."

sentences.zh: 遂迎立道入，出奇寶為賄，立道一無所受，但要日燇入朝。

translations.literal: He then welcomed Lidao in and produced rare treasures as bribes; Lidao accepted none of them and only demanded that Rizhuan come to court.
translations.idiomatic: He welcomed Lidao inside and offered rare treasures as gifts, but Lidao refused them all and required only that Rizhuan come to court.

sentences.zh: 日燇曰：「貪生畏死，人之常情，誠有詔貸以不死，臣將何辭。

translations.literal: Rizhuan said: "Clinging to life and fearing death are the common feelings of men; if there were truly an edict sparing me from death, what could this subject refuse?"
translations.idiomatic: Rizhuan said, "Clinging to life and fearing death are human nature. If there were truly an edict sparing my life, how could I refuse?"

sentences.zh: 」乃先遣其臣阮代之、何惟岩等隨立道上表謝罪，修歲貢之禮如初，且言所以願朝之意。

translations.literal: He then first sent his ministers Ruan Daizhi, He Weiyan, and others to accompany Lidao in submitting a memorial of confession, restored the annual tribute ritual as before, and stated the reasons for his wish to attend court.
translations.idiomatic: He first sent ministers Ruan Daizhi and He Weiyan with Lidao to submit a memorial of confession, restored the annual tribute as before, and explained his wish to attend court.

sentences.zh: 廷臣有害其功者，以為必先朝而後赦。

translations.literal: Court ministers who begrudged his achievement held that he must first attend court and only afterward be pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Some court ministers, jealous of his success, insisted that Rizhuan must come to court before any pardon could be granted.

sentences.zh: 日燇懼，卒不敢至，議者惜之。

translations.literal: Rizhuan was afraid and in the end did not dare come; those who discussed the matter regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: Rizhuan was afraid and never came. Commentators regretted the lost opportunity.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，遣立道奉使按行兩浙，尋以為四川南道宣慰使，遷陝西漢中道肅政廉訪使。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year Lidao was sent on mission to inspect the Two Zhe circuits; soon he was made pacification commissioner of Sichuan South Circuit and transferred to be surveillance commissioner of the Integrity and Uprightness Office on Shaanxi's Hanzhong Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year Lidao was sent to inspect the Two Zhe circuits. He was soon made pacification commissioner of Sichuan South Circuit and then surveillance commissioner on Shaanxi's Hanzhong Circuit.

sentences.zh: 三十年，皇曾孫松山封梁王，出鎮雲南。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year the emperor's great-grandson Songshan was enfeoffed as Prince of Liang and went out to govern Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year the emperor's great-grandson Songshan was enfeoffed as Prince of Liang and sent to govern Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 大德二年，廷議求舊臣可為梁王輔行者，立道遂以陝西行台侍御史拜雲南行省參政。

translations.literal: In the second year of Dade the court discussed seeking an old minister who could assist the Prince of Liang; Lidao was then appointed from Shaanxi Regional Secretariat associate censor to be regional secretary councillor of Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: In Dade 2 the court sought a veteran minister to assist the Prince of Liang. Lidao was promoted from associate censor on the Shaanxi regional secretariat to regional secretary councillor of Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 視事期月，卒於官。

translations.literal: After administering affairs for one month, he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: After one month in office he died.

sentences.zh: 立道凡三使安南，官雲南最久，頗得土人之心，為之立祠於鄯善城西。

translations.literal: Lidao in all made three missions to Annam and held office in Yunnan longest; he won the hearts of the native people considerably, and a shrine was built for him west of Shanshan city.
translations.idiomatic: Lidao served three times as envoy to Annam and held office in Yunnan longer than anyone else. He won the people's affection, and a shrine was built for him west of Shanshan.

sentences.zh: 立道所著詩文，有《效古集》、《平蜀總論》、《安南錄》、《雲南風土記》、《六昭通說》若干卷。

translations.literal: Lidao's writings in poetry and prose include several volumes such as Collected Imitations of Antiquity, General Discourse on Pacifying Shu, Record of Annam, Account of Yunnan Customs, and Exposition on Liutong.
translations.idiomatic: His writings included several volumes: Collected Imitations of Antiquity, General Discourse on Pacifying Shu, Record of Annam, Account of Yunnan Customs, and Exposition on Liutong.

sentences.zh: 子元，雲南行省左右司郎中。

translations.literal: His son Yuan was a langzhong of the left and right bureaus of the Yunnan Regional Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yuan served as langzhong in the left and right bureaus of the Yunnan regional secretariat.

sentences.zh: ○張庭珍庭瑞

translations.literal: Zhang Tingzhen and Tingrui
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tingzhen and Tingrui

sentences.zh: 世祖即位，自將北伐，以庭珍熟知西京入漠南路，遣立沙井諸驛，兼給糧運，俄授同僉土蕃經略使。

translations.literal: When the Founder took the throne he personally led the northern campaign; because Tingzhen was well acquainted with the route from Xijing into the desert south road, he was sent to establish the Shajing and other post stations and concurrently supply grain transport; soon he was appointed associate commissioner of the Tibetan Pacification Commission.
translations.idiomatic: When Kublai took the throne he led the northern campaign in person. Tingzhen knew the route from Xijing into the desert south road well, so he was sent to establish post stations at Shajing and elsewhere and supply grain transport. He was soon appointed associate commissioner of the Tibetan Pacification Commission.

sentences.zh: 至元六年，安南入貢不時，以庭珍為朝列大夫、安南國達魯花赤，佩金符，由吐蕃、大理諸蠻至於安南。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhiyuan, because Annam did not present tribute on schedule, Tingzhen was made Court Gentleman for Ordered Merit and darughachi of the state of Annam, wearing a gold tally, and went from Tibet, Dali, and the various tribes to Annam.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiyuan 6, when Annam failed to present tribute on time, Tingzhen was made Court Gentleman for Ordered Merit and darughachi of Annam, with a gold tally, and traveled through Tibet, Dali, and the tribal regions to reach Annam.

sentences.zh: 世子光昞立受昭，庭珍責之曰：「皇帝不欲以汝土地為郡縣，而聽汝稱籓，遣使喻旨，德至厚也。

translations.literal: The heir Guang Bing had just received the edict when Tingzhen reproved him: "The emperor does not wish to make your lands into prefectures and counties but allows you to call yourself a vassal; he sends envoys to convey his intent—his virtue is extremely great."
translations.idiomatic: When the heir Guang Bing received the edict, Tingzhen rebuked him: "The emperor does not wish to turn your land into prefectures and counties but allows you to remain a vassal. He sends envoys to explain his will—his grace is very great."

sentences.zh: 王猶與宋為脣齒，妄自尊大。

translations.literal: Yet the king still treats Song as lip and teeth and presumptuously holds himself high.
translations.idiomatic: Yet you still treat Song as your ally and presumptuously hold yourself high.

sentences.zh: 今百萬之師圍襄陽，拔在旦夕，席捲渡江，則宋亡矣，王將何恃？

translations.literal: Now a host of a million besieges Xiangyang; its fall is within days. When they sweep across the river, Song will perish—what will the king rely on?
translations.idiomatic: A million-man army now besieges Xiangyang. Its fall is imminent. When they sweep south across the Yangzi, Song will perish. What will you rely on then?

sentences.zh: 且雲南之兵不兩月可至汝境，覆汝宗祀有不難者，其審謀之。

translations.literal: Moreover, Yunnan's troops can reach your borders in less than two months; to overturn your ancestral sacrifices would not be difficult—consider this carefully."
translations.idiomatic: Yunnan's troops can reach your borders in less than two months. Overturning your ancestral line would not be difficult. Consider that carefully."

sentences.zh: 」光昞惶恐，下拜受詔，既而語庭珍曰：「聖天子憐我，而使者來多無禮，汝官朝列，我王也，相與抗禮，古有之乎？

translations.literal: Guang Bing was fearful and bowed to receive the edict; afterward he said to Tingzhen: "The sage Son of Heaven pities me, yet the envoys who come are mostly without courtesy. You hold court rank; I am a king—did antiquity ever have mutual refusal of precedence?"
translations.idiomatic: Guang Bing bowed in fear to receive the edict, then said to Tingzhen, "The sage Son of Heaven shows me mercy, yet your envoys are often rude. You hold court rank and I am a king—did antiquity ever allow equals to refuse precedence to each other?"

sentences.zh: 」庭珍曰：「有之。

translations.literal: Tingzhen said: "It did."
translations.idiomatic: Tingzhen said, "It did."

sentences.zh: 王人雖微，序於諸侯之上。

translations.literal: A royal envoy, though low in rank, takes precedence above the feudal lords.
translations.idiomatic: A royal envoy, though low in rank, takes precedence over feudal lords.

sentences.zh: 」光昞曰：「汝過益州，見雲南王拜否？

translations.literal: Guang Bing said: "When you passed Yizhou, did you bow to the Prince of Yunnan?"
translations.idiomatic: Guang Bing said, "When you passed Yizhou, did you bow to the Prince of Yunnan?"

sentences.zh: 」庭珍曰：「雲南王，天子之子，汝蠻夷小邦，特假以王號，豈得比雲南王？

translations.literal: Tingzhen said: "The Prince of Yunnan is the Son of Heaven's son; you are a petty barbarian state granted a king's title in name only—how can you be compared to the Prince of Yunnan?"
translations.idiomatic: Tingzhen said, "The Prince of Yunnan is the Son of Heaven's son. You are a petty frontier state granted a king's title in name only. How can you compare with the Prince of Yunnan?"

sentences.zh: 況天子命我為安南之長，位居汝上耶！

translations.literal: Moreover, the Son of Heaven has appointed me chief over Annam—my position is above yours!"
translations.idiomatic: Besides, the Son of Heaven has appointed me chief over Annam. My rank is above yours!"

sentences.zh: 」光昞曰：「既稱大國，何索吾犀象？

translations.literal: Guang Bing said: "If you call yourselves a great state, why demand my rhinoceros horns and elephants?"
translations.idiomatic: Guang Bing said, "If you call yourselves a great power, why demand my rhinoceros horns and elephants?"

sentences.zh: 」庭珍曰： 「貢獻方物，籓臣職也。

translations.literal: Tingzhen said: "Presenting local products is a vassal minister's duty."
translations.idiomatic: Tingzhen said, "Presenting local products is a vassal's duty."

sentences.zh: 」光

translations.literal: Guang
translations.idiomatic: Guang

sentences.zh: 昞無以對，益慚憤，使衛兵露刃環立以恐庭珍。

translations.literal: Bing had nothing to reply and grew all the more ashamed and angry; he had palace guards bare their blades and stand in a ring to frighten Tingzhen.
translations.idiomatic: Bing had no answer and grew more ashamed and angry. He had guards bare their swords and surround Tingzhen to intimidate him.

sentences.zh: 庭珍解所佩弓刀，坦臥室中曰：「聽汝何為！

translations.literal: Tingzhen unfastened the bow and knife at his belt, lay calmly in his room, and said: "Do as you please!"
translations.idiomatic: Tingzhen removed his bow and knife, lay down calmly in his room, and said, "Do as you please!"

sentences.zh: 」光昞及群下皆服。

translations.literal: Guang Bing and all his subordinates submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Guang Bing and all his followers submitted.

sentences.zh: 明年，遣使隨庭珍入貢。

translations.literal: The next year he sent envoys to accompany Tingzhen in presenting tribute.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he sent envoys to accompany Tingzhen to court with tribute.

sentences.zh: 庭珍見帝，以所對光昞之言聞，帝大悅，命付翰​​林承旨王磐紀之。

translations.literal: Tingzhen saw the emperor and reported what he had said to Guang Bing; the emperor was greatly pleased and ordered Hanlin Academician Wang Pan to record it.
translations.idiomatic: When Tingzhen saw the emperor and reported his exchange with Guang Bing, the emperor was delighted and had Hanlin Academician Wang Pan record it.

sentences.zh: 授襄陽行省郎中。

translations.literal: He was appointed langzhong of the Xiangyang Regional Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed langzhong of the Xiangyang regional secretariat.

sentences.zh: 與阿里海牙從數騎抵襄陽南門，呼宋將呂文煥語曰：「我師所攻，無不取者，汝孤城路絕，外無一兵之援，而欲以死守求空名，如闔郡之人何！

translations.literal: With Alihaiya he rode with a few horsemen to Xiangyang's south gate and called to the Song general Lü Wenhuan: "Every place Our army attacks is taken. Your isolated city has its roads cut off and not a single soldier's aid from outside, yet you wish to die in a stubborn defense for an empty name—what of the people of the whole commandery!"
translations.idiomatic: With Alihaiya he rode with a few men to Xiangyang's south gate and called to the Song general Lü Wenhuan, "Our army takes every place it attacks. Your city is isolated, cut off, with no reinforcements, yet you would die in a stubborn defense for an empty reputation. What of all the people in your commandery?"

sentences.zh: 汝宜早圖之。

translations.literal: You should plan early for this.
translations.idiomatic: You should decide soon."

sentences.zh: 」文煥帳前將田世英、曹彪執其總管武榮來降，文煥益孤，明日，遣黑楊都統來議納款。

translations.literal: Wenhuan's front-camp generals Tian Shiying and Cao Biao seized their director-general Wu Rong and came to surrender; Wenhuan was all the more isolated. The next day he sent Commander Heiyang to discuss submitting.
translations.idiomatic: Wenhuan's generals Tian Shiying and Cao Biao seized their director-general Wu Rong and surrendered. Wenhuan was left more isolated. The next day he sent Commander Heiyang to negotiate surrender.

sentences.zh: 將遣之還報，庭珍曰：「彼來，或以計覘我，未能必其果降。

translations.literal: They were about to send him back with a report when Tingzhen said: "He has come—perhaps to spy on us with a stratagem; we cannot be sure they will truly surrender."
translations.idiomatic: They were about to send him back when Tingzhen said, "He may have come to spy on us. We cannot be sure they will truly surrender."

sentences.zh: 此人呂氏腹心，不如留之，以伐其謀。

translations.literal: This man is the Lü clan's trusted inner man; better to detain him and thwart their plans."
translations.idiomatic: This man is Lü's trusted confidant. Better to keep him and thwart their plans."

sentences.zh: 」元帥阿術然之，乃留不遣。

translations.literal: Marshal Aju approved and detained him without sending him back.
translations.idiomatic: Marshal Aju agreed and kept him from returning.

sentences.zh: 又明日，文煥舉城降。

translations.literal: On the day after that, Wenhuan surrendered the whole city.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Wenhuan surrendered the entire city.

sentences.zh: 以功遷中順大夫、遙授知歸德府行樞密院經歷。

translations.literal: For merit he was promoted to Grand Master of Palace Accordance and given remote appointment as administrator of the Guid Prefecture Branch Secretariat of the Privy Council.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was promoted to Grand Master of Palace Accordance and given remote appointment as administrator of the Guid Prefecture branch secretariat of the Privy Council.

sentences.zh: 諸軍南渡，復為行省郎中，俄授金虎符、襄陽總管，兼府尹，改郢、复二州達魯花赤。

translations.literal: When the armies crossed south, he again became regional secretariat langzhong; soon he was given a gold tiger tally as Xiangyang director-general, concurrently prefect, and was changed to darughachi of Ying and Fu prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: When the armies crossed the Yangzi he again became regional secretariat langzhong, then received a gold tiger tally as Xiangyang director-general and prefect, and later served as darughachi of Ying and Fu prefectures.

sentences.zh: 宋平，遷平江路達魯花赤，改同知浙東宣慰使司事。

translations.literal: When Song was pacified, he was transferred to be darughachi of Pingjiang Circuit and changed to associate commissioner of the Zhedong Pacification Commission.
translations.idiomatic: After the pacification of Song he became darughachi of Pingjiang Circuit, then associate commissioner of the Zhedong Pacification Commission.

sentences.zh: 未行，拜大司農卿。

translations.literal: Before he could depart, he was appointed Grand Minister of Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could take up the post he was appointed Grand Minister of Agriculture.

sentences.zh: 連居親憂，起復南京路總管，兼開封府尹。

translations.literal: He observed mourning for parents in succession, was recalled from mourning to be Nanjing Route director-general, and concurrently Kaifeng prefect.
translations.idiomatic: After successive periods of mourning for his parents he was recalled to serve as Nanjing Route director-general and concurrently Kaifeng prefect.

sentences.zh: 開封有控鶴軍士十餘人，賃大宅聚居，縱橫街陌。

translations.literal: In Kaifeng more than ten Crane-Control Army soldiers rented a large house and lived together, swaggering through the streets.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaifeng more than ten Crane-Control Army soldiers rented a large house and lived together, swaggering through the streets.

sentences.zh: 庭珍始至，察其必為盜，急捕之，得寶玩、器服、子女滿室，窮索其黨，俱殺之，民以為神。

translations.literal: When Tingzhen first arrived, he perceived they must be robbers and swiftly arrested them; precious objects, vessels and robes, and women and children filled the rooms; he traced their gang to the end and killed them all; the people thought him divine.
translations.idiomatic: When Tingzhen arrived he saw they must be robbers and arrested them at once. Their rooms were full of loot, goods, and captive women and children. He tracked down the whole gang and executed them all. The people regarded him as miraculous.

sentences.zh: 河決，灌太康，漂溺千里，庭珍括商人漁子船及縛木為筏，載糗糧四出救之，全活甚眾。

translations.literal: The river burst its banks and inundated Taikang; people drowned and drifted for a thousand li; Tingzhen requisitioned merchants' and fishermen's boats and bound wood into rafts, loaded dry provisions, and went out in all directions to rescue them; very many were saved alive.
translations.idiomatic: When the river burst its banks and flooded Taikang for a thousand li, Tingzhen requisitioned merchant and fishing boats and built rafts, loaded provisions, and sent rescue parties in all directions. He saved a great many lives.

sentences.zh: 水入善利門，庭珍親督夫運薪土捍之，不能止，乃頹城為堰。

translations.literal: Water entered the Shanli Gate; Tingzhen personally supervised laborers transporting firewood and earth to hold it back but could not stop it, and so demolished the city wall to make a dike.
translations.idiomatic: When water entered the Shanli Gate, Tingzhen personally supervised workers hauling timber and earth to hold it back. When that failed, he demolished part of the city wall to build a dike.

sentences.zh: 水既退，即發民增外防百三十里，人免水憂。

translations.literal: When the water had receded, he immediately mobilized the people to extend the outer defenses for one hundred thirty li, and the people were spared flood calamity.
translations.idiomatic: After the flood receded he mobilized the people to extend the outer defenses for 130 li, sparing them further flood damage.

sentences.zh: 俄卒於官。

translations.literal: Soon he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died in office.

sentences.zh: 庭珍性清慎，丞相伯顏嘗語人曰：「諸將渡江，無不荒貪，唯我與國寶始終自守。

translations.literal: Tingzhen's nature was pure and cautious; Chancellor Bayan once said to people: "Of all the generals who crossed the river, none failed to grow dissolute and greedy—only Guobao and I always kept ourselves in check."
translations.idiomatic: Tingzhen was upright and cautious by nature. Chancellor Bayan once said, "Of all the generals who crossed the Yangzi, none escaped dissipation and greed—only Guobao and I held ourselves in check throughout."

sentences.zh: 」聞者以為知言。

translations.literal: Those who heard it considered it perceptive speech.
translations.idiomatic: Those who heard it agreed he spoke the truth.

sentences.zh: 弟庭瑞。

translations.literal: His younger brother Tingrui.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother was Tingrui.

sentences.zh: 庭瑞字天表，幼以功業自許，兵法、地志、星曆、卜筮無不推究，以宿衛從憲宗伐蜀為先鋒。

translations.literal: Tingrui, courtesy name Tianbiao, in youth pledged himself to achievement; military methods, geographical treatises, astronomy and calendrics, divination—none did he fail to investigate thoroughly; as a palace guard he followed Emperor Xianzong in the campaign against Shu as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Tingrui, courtesy name Tianbiao, aspired to great deeds from youth and studied military science, geography, astronomy, and divination thoroughly. As a palace guard he followed Emperor Xianzong's campaign against Shu as vanguard.

sentences.zh: 中統二年，授元帥府參議，留戍青居。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhongtong he was appointed councilor of the Marshal's Headquarters and remained to garrison Qingju.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhongtong 2 he was appointed councilor of the marshal's headquarters and garrisoned Qingju.

sentences.zh: 諸軍攻開州、達州，庭端將兵築城虎嘯山，扼二州路。

translations.literal: When the armies attacked Kaizhou and Dazhou, Tingrui led troops to build a fort on Tiger's Roar Mountain and choke the routes of the two prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: When the armies attacked Kaizhou and Dazhou, Tingrui built a fort on Tiger's Roar Mountain to block the routes between the two prefectures.

sentences.zh: 宋將夏貴以師數万圍之，城當砲，皆穿，築柵守之，柵壞，乃依大樹張牛馬皮以拒砲。

translations.literal: The Song general Xia Gui surrounded it with an army of tens of thousands; the city was struck by catapults and all pierced through; they built palisades to defend, and when the palisades were ruined they relied on great trees and stretched ox and horse hides to resist the catapults.
translations.idiomatic: The Song general Xia Gui besieged it with tens of thousands of men. Catapult shots pierced the walls. They built palisades, and when those failed they stretched ox and horse hides from great trees to block the stones.

sentences.zh: 貴以城中人飲於澗，外絕其水。

translations.literal: Gui, because the people in the city drank from the stream, cut off their water from outside.
translations.idiomatic: Gui cut off the stream because the garrison drew its water from it.

sentences.zh: 庭瑞取人畜溲沸煮之，瀉土中以洩臭，人日飲數合，脣皆瘡裂。

translations.literal: Tingrui took human and animal urine, boiled it, poured it into earth to release the stench, and the people drank several he each day; all their lips were cracked with sores.
translations.idiomatic: Tingrui boiled human and animal urine, poured it through earth to reduce the stench, and had the men drink a few he a day. Their lips cracked with sores.

sentences.zh: 堅守踰月，援兵不敢進。

translations.literal: They held firm for more than a month, and relief troops did not dare advance.
translations.idiomatic: They held out for more than a month while relief troops dared not advance.

sentences.zh: 庭瑞度宋兵稍懈，三分其兵，夜劫貴營，宋兵驚潰，殺都統欒俊、雍貴、胡世雄等五人，斬千餘級，庭瑞亦被傷數處。

translations.literal: Tingrui judged the Song army slightly slackened, divided his troops in three, and by night raided Gui's camp; the Song army fled in panic; he killed the commanders Luan Jun, Yong Gui, Hu Shixiong, and five others, and beheaded more than a thousand; Tingrui also received wounds in several places.
translations.idiomatic: When Tingrui judged the Song army had slackened, he divided his force in three and raided Gui's camp by night. The Song troops fled in panic. He killed commanders Luan Jun, Yong Gui, Hu Shixiong, and others—five in all—and beheaded more than a thousand men. Tingrui himself was wounded in several places.

sentences.zh: 以功授奉議大夫、知高唐州，改濮州尹，遷陝西四川道按察副使。

translations.literal: For merit he was appointed Grand Master of Court Discussion and made prefect of Gaotang; he was changed to Puzhou prefect and transferred to be associate surveillance commissioner of the Shaanxi-Sichuan Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was made Grand Master of Court Discussion and prefect of Gaotang, then Puzhou prefect, and later associate surveillance commissioner on the Shaanxi-Sichuan circuit.

sentences.zh: 政過於猛，上官弗便，陷以罪，徙四川屯田經略副使。

translations.literal: His government was overly harsh; superiors found it inconvenient and framed him with a crime, transferring him to be associate commissioner of the Sichuan Garrison-Farming Commission.
translations.idiomatic: His rule was too harsh for his superiors' liking. They framed him on a charge and transferred him to associate commissioner of the Sichuan garrison-farming commission.

sentences.zh: 東西川行樞密院發兵圍重慶，朝廷知庭瑞練習軍事，換成都總管，佩虎符，舟楫兵仗糧儲皆倚以辦。

translations.literal: The Eastern and Western Sichuan Branch Privy Council sent troops to besiege Chongqing; the court knew Tingrui was practiced in military affairs and transferred him to be Chengdu director-general, wearing a tiger tally; boats, weapons, and grain stores all relied on him to arrange.
translations.idiomatic: When the Eastern and Western Sichuan branch privy council besieged Chongqing, the court knew Tingrui was skilled in military affairs and made him Chengdu director-general with a tiger tally. Boats, weapons, and grain stores all depended on him.

sentences.zh: 蜀平，升諸蠻夷部宣慰使，甚得蠻夷心。

translations.literal: When Shu was pacified, he was promoted to pacification commissioner of the various tribal departments and won the hearts of the tribes deeply.
translations.idiomatic: After the pacification of Shu he was promoted to pacification commissioner over the tribal departments and won their deep loyalty.

sentences.zh: 碉門羌與婦人老幼入市，爭價殺人，碉門魚通司擊其人。

translations.literal: Qiang of Diaomen went to market with women, old people, and children; in haggling over prices they killed a man; the Diaomen Yutong Office struck the offenders.
translations.idiomatic: Qiang from Diaomen went to market with women, children, and elders. A price dispute led to killing, and the Diaomen Yutong Office arrested the offenders.

sentences.zh: 羌酋怒，斷繩橋，謀入劫之。

translations.literal: The Qiang chieftain was angry, cut the rope bridge, and plotted to enter and raid them.
translations.idiomatic: The Qiang chieftain was furious, cut the rope bridge, and planned a raid.

sentences.zh: 魚通司來告急，左丞汪惟正問計，庭瑞曰：「羌俗暴悍，以鬥殺為勇。

translations.literal: The Yutong Office came with an urgent report; Left Chancellor Wang Weizheng asked for a plan; Tingrui said: "Qiang custom is violent and fierce; they take killing in combat as courage."
translations.idiomatic: The Yutong Office reported an emergency. Left Chancellor Wang Weizheng asked for advice. Tingrui said, "The Qiang are violent by custom and take killing as courage."

sentences.zh: 今如蜂毒一人，而即以門牆之寇待之，不可。

translations.literal: Now, as when a bee stings one man, to treat them at once as enemies at the gate cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: If one bee stings a man, you cannot treat the whole hive as an enemy at the gate. That will not do.

sentences.zh: 宜遣使往諭禍福，彼悟，當自回矣。

translations.literal: It is fitting to send an envoy to explain fortune and calamity; when they understand, they will surely withdraw of themselves."
translations.idiomatic: Send an envoy to explain the consequences. Once they understand, they will withdraw on their own."

sentences.zh: 」惟正曰：「使者無過於君。

translations.literal: Weizheng said: "No envoy could be better than you."
translations.idiomatic: Weizheng said, "No one is better suited to be the envoy than you."

sentences.zh: 」遂從數騎，抵羌界。

translations.literal: He then went with a few horsemen and reached the Qiang border.
translations.idiomatic: He rode out with a few men to the Qiang border.

sentences.zh: 羌陳兵以待，庭瑞進前語之曰：「殺人償死，羌與中國之法同，有司擊諸人，欲以為見證耳。

translations.literal: The Qiang arrayed troops to await him; Tingrui advanced and said to them: "Killing a man is repaid with death—the Qiang and the Middle Kingdom share the same law; the officials struck those men only to use them as witnesses."
translations.idiomatic: The Qiang drew up their troops. Tingrui rode forward and said, "Killing is repaid with death—the Qiang and China share the same law. The officials arrested those men only as witnesses."

sentences.zh: 而汝即肆無禮，如行省聞於朝，召近郡兵，空汝巢穴矣。

translations.literal: Yet you immediately act without courtesy; if the regional secretariat reports to court and summons troops from nearby commanderies, your nests will be emptied."
translations.idiomatic: Yet you act without courtesy. If the regional secretariat reports to court and summons nearby troops, your settlements will be destroyed."

sentences.zh: 」其酋長棄槍弩羅拜曰：「我近者生裂羊脾卜之，視肉之文理何如，則吉其兆，曰：'有白馬將軍來，可不勞兵而罷。

translations.literal: Their chieftain cast aside spears and crossbows and bowed in a circle, saying: "I recently split a sheep's spleen alive for divination and examined the grain of the flesh—its omen was auspicious, saying: 'A white-horse general will come; troops need not be mobilized and matters will cease.'"
translations.idiomatic: Their chieftain cast aside his weapons and bowed in a circle. "I recently divined by splitting a sheep's spleen," he said. "The omen was auspicious: 'A white-horse general will come, and the trouble will end without fighting.'"

sentences.zh: '今公馬果白，敢不從命。

translations.literal: Now your horse is indeed white—we dare not disobey your command."
translations.idiomatic: Your horse is indeed white. How could we disobey?"

sentences.zh: 」乃論殺人者，餘盡縱遣之。

translations.literal: He then tried the killers; the rest were all released and sent away.
translations.idiomatic: He tried the killers and released the rest.

sentences.zh: 遂與約，自今交市者，以碉門為界，無相出入。

translations.literal: He then made an agreement that from now on those who traded would take Diaomen as the boundary and not cross in and out of each other's territory.
translations.idiomatic: They agreed that from then on trade would use Diaomen as the boundary and neither side would cross without permission.

sentences.zh: 官買蜀茶，增價鬻於羌，人以為患。

translations.literal: The government bought Shu tea and sold it to the Qiang at raised prices; people regarded it as a hardship.
translations.idiomatic: The government bought Shu tea and resold it to the Qiang at inflated prices, which the people found oppressive.

sentences.zh: 庭瑞更變引法，使每引納二緡，而付文券與民，聽其自市於羌，羌、蜀便之。

translations.literal: Tingrui changed the transport regulations so that each transport permit paid two strings of cash, and written certificates were given to the people, allowing them to trade with the Qiang on their own; Qiang and Shu both found it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Tingrui reformed the transport regulations: each permit paid two strings of cash, the people received certificates, and they were free to trade with the Qiang themselves. Both sides benefited.

sentences.zh: 先時，運糧由楊山溯江，往往覆陷，庭瑞始立屯田，人得免患。

translations.literal: Formerly grain transport went upriver from Yangshan and often capsized and sank; Tingrui first established garrison farming, and the people were spared the calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly grain transport upriver from Yangshan often ended in shipwreck. Tingrui established garrison farms so the people were spared that hardship.

sentences.zh: 都掌蠻叛，蠻善飛槍，聯松枝為牌自蔽，行省命庭瑞討之。

translations.literal: The Duzhang tribes rebelled; the tribes were skilled with flying spears and joined pine branches into shields to protect themselves; the regional secretariat ordered Tingrui to punish them.
translations.idiomatic: The Duzhang tribes rebelled. They were skilled with throwing spears and used pine-branch shields for protection. The regional secretariat ordered Tingrui to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 庭瑞所射矢，出其牌半竿，蠻驚曰：「何物弓矢如此之力！

translations.literal: An arrow Tingrui shot passed halfway through their shield; the tribes were alarmed and said: "What sort of bow and arrow has such force!"
translations.idiomatic: An arrow Tingrui shot passed halfway through their shield. The tribes cried in alarm, "What bow and arrow has such force!"

sentences.zh: 」即請服。

translations.literal: They immediately asked to submit.
translations.idiomatic: They immediately asked to submit.

sentences.zh: 惟斬其酋德蘭酉等十餘人，而招復其餘民。

translations.literal: Only their chiefs Delanyou and more than ten others were beheaded, while the rest of the people were summoned back and restored.
translations.idiomatic: He executed only their chiefs Delanyou and a dozen others and brought the rest of the people back under control.

sentences.zh: 授敘州等處蠻夷部宣撫使，改潭州路總管。

translations.literal: He was appointed pacification commissioner of the tribal departments of Xuzhou and other places and changed to be director-general of Tanzhou Route.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed pacification commissioner over the tribal departments of Xuzhou and neighboring areas, then made director-general of Tanzhou Route.

sentences.zh: 時湖廣省臣方剝民為功，庭瑞知不可拒，乃辭歸關中。

translations.literal: At that time Huguang regional secretariat ministers were stripping the people to make achievements; Tingrui knew he could not refuse and so resigned and returned to Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Huguang regional secretariat ministers were exploiting the people for credit. Tingrui knew he could not resist them and resigned to return to Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 三年，思成都，遂從漢中分家奴往居焉。

translations.literal: Three years later, longing for Chengdu, he took household slaves from Hanzhong and went to live there.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later, missing Chengdu, he took household slaves from Hanzhong and went to live there.

sentences.zh: 以疾卒。

translations.literal: He died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He died of illness.

sentences.zh: 庭瑞初屯青居，其土多橘，時中州艱得蜀藥，其價倍常。

translations.literal: When Tingrui first garrisoned Qingju, its soil had many oranges; at that time the central plains found it hard to obtain Shu medicines, and their price was double the usual.
translations.idiomatic: When Tingrui first garrisoned Qingju, the region had many orange trees. Medicines from Shu were scarce in the central plains and sold at double the usual price.

sentences.zh: 庭瑞課閒卒，日入橘皮若干升儲之，人莫曉也。

translations.literal: Tingrui assigned idle soldiers to bring in several sheng of orange peel each day for storage; no one understood why.
translations.idiomatic: Tingrui had idle soldiers collect several sheng of orange peel each day. No one understood why.

sentences.zh: 賈人有喪其資不能歸者，人給橘皮一石，得錢以濟，莫不感之。

translations.literal: When merchants lost their capital and could not return home, each was given a shi of orange peel and obtained money to get by; none failed to be moved.
translations.idiomatic: When merchants lost their capital and could not return home, each received a shi of orange peel worth enough money to get by. All were deeply grateful.

sentences.zh: 家有愛妾，一日見老人與之語，乃其父也，妾以告庭瑞。

translations.literal: He had a beloved concubine; one day she saw an old man speaking with her—it was her father—and the concubine told Tingrui.
translations.idiomatic: He had a beloved concubine who one day saw an old man speaking with her—it was her father—and she told Tingrui.

sentences.zh: 召視之，其貌甚似，問：「欲得汝女歸耶？

translations.literal: He summoned and looked at him; his appearance was very similar, and asked: "Do you wish to take your daughter back?"
translations.idiomatic: Tingrui summoned him. The resemblance was striking. "Do you want your daughter back?" he asked.

sentences.zh: 」其人以為幸侍左右，非敢求與歸。

translations.literal: The man thought it fortunate enough to serve at his side and did not dare ask to take her back.
translations.idiomatic: The man said he was fortunate enough that she served Tingrui and did not dare ask for her return.

sentences.zh: 庭瑞曰：「汝女居吾家，不過群婢，歸嫁則良人矣。

translations.literal: Tingrui said: "Your daughter in my house is no more than one of the maidservants; if she returns to marry, she will have a proper husband."
translations.idiomatic: Tingrui said, "In my house your daughter is only one of many maidservants. If she returns home to marry, she will have a proper husband."

sentences.zh: 」盡取奩裝書券還之，時人以為難。

translations.literal: He took all her trousseau, documents, and certificates and returned them; people of the time considered it a difficult virtue.
translations.idiomatic: He returned all her trousseau, documents, and certificates. People of the time admired the difficulty of that act.

sentences.zh: ○張惠

translations.literal: Zhang Hui
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hui

sentences.zh: 張惠，字廷傑，成都新繁人，宋尚書右僕射商英之裔孫也。

translations.literal: Zhang Hui, courtesy name Tingjie, a man of Xinfan in Chengdu, was a descendant of Song Right Vice Director of the Secretariat Shang Ying.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hui, courtesy name Tingjie, of Xinfan in Chengdu, was a descendant of the Song Right Vice Director of the Secretariat Shang Ying.

sentences.zh: 其先徙居青河，後徙蜀。

translations.literal: His ancestors first moved to Qinghe, then later moved to Shu.
translations.idiomatic: His family first moved to Qinghe and later to Shu.

sentences.zh: 歲丙申，惠年十四，兵入蜀，被俘至杭海。

translations.literal: In the year bingshen, Hui at age fourteen, when troops entered Shu, was captured and taken to Hanghai.
translations.idiomatic: In the bingshen year, when Hui was fourteen, the armies entered Shu and he was captured and taken to Hanghai.

sentences.zh: 居數年，盡通諸國語，丞相蒙速速愛而薦之，入侍世祖籓邸。

translations.literal: After several years he mastered all the languages of the various states; Chancellor Meng Susu favored him and recommended him, and he entered service in the Founder's princely residence.
translations.idiomatic: After several years he mastered the languages of many states. Chancellor Meng Susu favored him and recommended him to serve in Kublai's princely household.

sentences.zh: 以謹敏稱，賜名兀魯忽訥特。

translations.literal: He was known for prudence and quickness and was granted the name Ulugunet.
translations.idiomatic: Known for prudence and quickness, he was given the Mongol name Ulugunet.

sentences.zh: 世祖即位，授燕京宣慰副使。

translations.literal: When the Founder took the throne, he was appointed associate pacification commissioner of Yanjing.
translations.idiomatic: When Kublai took the throne he was appointed associate pacification commissioner of Yanjing.

sentences.zh: 為政寬簡，奏免分數錢，罷硝鹼局。

translations.literal: His government was lenient and simple; he memorialized to abolish the apportioned cash levy and abolished the saltpeter and alkali office.
translations.idiomatic: His rule was lenient and simple. He memorialized to abolish apportioned cash levies and shut down the saltpeter and alkali monopoly office.

sentences.zh: 俄遷侍中。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to be Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 至元元年冬，拜參知政事，行省山東。

translations.literal: In the winter of the first year of Zhiyuan he was appointed Associate Administrator of Affairs and acted as regional secretariat of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of Zhiyuan 1 he was appointed associate administrator of affairs for the Shandong regional secretariat.

sentences.zh: 以銀贖俘囚二百餘家為民，其不能歸者，使為僧，建寺居之。

translations.literal: With silver he ransomed more than two hundred families of captive prisoners to become commoners; those who could not return he had become monks and built a temple to house them.
translations.idiomatic: He used silver to ransom more than two hundred captive families and restore them as commoners. Those who could not return home he made monks and built a temple to house them.

sentences.zh: 李璮之亂，山東民被軍士虜掠者甚眾，惠至，大括軍中，悉縱之。

translations.literal: In Li Tan's rebellion very many Shandong commoners were seized and plundered by soldiers; when Hui arrived, he made a great search through the army and released them all.
translations.idiomatic: During Li Tan's rebellion many Shandong civilians were seized by soldiers. When Hui arrived he searched the army thoroughly and released them all.

sentences.zh: 又奏選良吏，去冗官，以蘇民瘼。

translations.literal: He also memorialized to select good officials, remove redundant offices, and relieve the people's hardships.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized to select capable officials, remove redundant posts, and relieve the people's hardships.

sentences.zh: 遷制國用司副使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be vice commissioner of the State Revenue Office.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to vice commissioner of the State Revenue Office.

sentences.zh: 會改制國用司為尚書省，拜參知政事，遷中書左丞，進右丞。

translations.literal: When the State Revenue Office was changed into the Ministry, he was appointed Associate Administrator, transferred to Left Chancellor of the Secretariat, and advanced to Right Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: When the State Revenue Office became the Ministry, he was made associate administrator, then left chancellor of the Secretariat, and finally right chancellor.

sentences.zh: 伯顏帥師伐宋，十二年夏，詔惠主其饋餉，凡江淮錢穀皆領之。

translations.literal: Bayan commanded the army to attack Song; in the summer of the twelfth year an edict ordered Hui to take charge of its provisions; all money and grain of Jiang and Huai came under his direction.
translations.idiomatic: When Bayan commanded the campaign against Song, an edict in the summer of the twelfth year put Hui in charge of provisions. All revenue and grain from the Jiang-Huai region came under his control.

sentences.zh: 十三年春，宋降，伯顏命惠與參知政事阿剌罕等入城，按閱府庫版籍，收其太廟及景靈宮禮樂器物、冊寶、郊天儀仗。

translations.literal: In the spring of the thirteenth year Song surrendered; Bayan ordered Hui together with Associate Administrator Alahan and others to enter the city, inspect the treasuries and registers, and collect the ritual vessels, music instruments, registers and seals of the Imperial Ancestral Temple and Jingling Palace, and the ceremonial regalia for suburban sacrifice to Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the thirteenth year Song surrendered. Bayan ordered Hui, Associate Administrator Alahan, and others to enter the city, inspect the treasuries and registers, and collect the ritual vessels, music instruments, registers, seals, and suburban-sacrifice regalia from the Imperial Ancestral Temple and Jingling Palace.

sentences.zh: 籍江南民為工匠凡三十萬戶，惠選有藝業者僅十餘萬戶，餘悉奏還為民。

translations.literal: Jiangnan commoners were registered as artisans totaling three hundred thousand households; Hui selected those with skilled trades—only a little more than one hundred thousand households—and memorialized to return the rest as commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Three hundred thousand Jiangnan households were registered as artisans. Hui selected only those with real skills—about one hundred thousand households—and memorialized to return the rest to common status.

sentences.zh: 伯顏以宋主北還，俾惠居守。

translations.literal: Bayan, because the Song ruler was returning north, had Hui remain to guard the city.
translations.idiomatic: When Bayan took the Song ruler north, he left Hui to guard the city.

sentences.zh: 惠不待命，輒啟府庫封鑰，伯顏以聞，詔左丞相阿術、平章政事阿塔海詰之，徵還京師。

translations.literal: Hui, without awaiting orders, opened the treasury seals and keys; Bayan reported it; an edict ordered Left Chancellor Aju and Grand Councillor Atahai to investigate him, and he was summoned back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Without waiting for orders, Hui opened the sealed treasuries. Bayan reported it. An edict had Left Chancellor Aju and Grand Councillor Atahai investigate him, and he was recalled to the capital.

sentences.zh: 二十年，拜榮祿大夫、平章政事，行省揚州。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he was appointed Grand Master for Glorious Happiness and Grand Councillor, acting as regional secretariat of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year he was made Grand Master for Glorious Happiness and grand councillor for the Yangzhou regional secretariat.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，入朝，復命以平章政事行省杭州。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he entered court and was again ordered as grand councillor acting as regional secretariat of Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year he went to court and was again appointed grand councillor for the Hangzhou regional secretariat.

sentences.zh: 至無錫卒，年六十二。

translations.literal: He died at Wuxi at age sixty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died at Wuxi at the age of sixty-two.

sentences.zh: 惠所至有能聲，及老，頗以沉浮取譏。

translations.literal: Wherever Hui went he had a reputation for ability; in old age he drew considerable criticism for being unsteady.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever Hui served he won a reputation for ability, but in old age he drew criticism for being unsteady.

sentences.zh: 子遵誨。

translations.literal: His son Zunhui.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Zunhui.

sentences.zh: ○劉好禮

translations.literal: Liu Haoli
translations.idiomatic: Liu Haoli

sentences.zh: 劉好禮，字敬之，汴梁祥符人。

translations.literal: Liu Haoli, courtesy name Jingzhi, a man of Xiangfu in Bianliang.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Haoli, courtesy name Jingzhi, was from Xiangfu in Bianliang.

sentences.zh: 父仲澤，金大理評事，遙授同知許州，徙家保定之完州。

translations.literal: His father was Zhongze, an evaluating clerk of the Dali Court under Jin, remotely appointed associate prefect of Xuzhou; the family moved to Wanzhou in Baoding.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhongze had served Jin as an evaluating clerk in the Dali Court and held a remote appointment as associate prefect of Xuzhou; the family later moved to Wanzhou in Baoding.

sentences.zh: 好禮幼有志，知讀書，通國言，憲宗時廉訪府辟為參議。

translations.literal: Haoli had ambition from youth, knew how to read, was fluent in the national language; during Emperor Xianzong's reign the surveillance commission recruited him as deliberator.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood Haoli was ambitious and studious, literate and fluent in the national language; under Emperor Xianzong the surveillance commission recruited him as deliberator.

sentences.zh: 歲乙卯，改永興府達魯花赤。

translations.literal: In the yimao year he was changed to darughachi of Yongxing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the yimao year he was reassigned as darughachi of Yongxing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 至元元年，以侍儀廉希逸薦召見，言舉人材數事，稱旨。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhiyuan, recommended by Ceremonial Attendant Lian Xiyi, he was summoned for an audience; he spoke on several matters concerning the recommendation of talent, and his words pleased the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiyuan 1, on the recommendation of Ceremonial Attendant Lian Xiyi, he was summoned to court and spoke on several matters of recruiting talent; the emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 五年，應詔建言：「凡有司奏請，宜先啟皇太子，俾得閱習庶政，以為社稷生民之福。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, responding to an edict he offered advice: "All offices submitting memorials should first report to the Crown Prince, so that he may practice routine governance—a blessing for the altars of state and the people."
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, answering an imperial summons, he advised: "All offices submitting memorials should first report them to the Crown Prince so he may practice routine governance—a blessing for the realm and its people."

sentences.zh: 陝西重地，宜封皇子諸王以鎮之。

translations.literal: Shaanxi is a vital region; imperial sons and princes should be enfeoffed to guard it.
translations.idiomatic: Shaanxi is a vital region; imperial sons and princes should be enfeoffed there to hold it.

sentences.zh: 創築都城，宜給直以市民地。

translations.literal: When constructing the new capital, fair payment should be given for land taken from commoners.
translations.idiomatic: When building the new capital, fair compensation should be paid for land taken from commoners.

sentences.zh: 選格不宜以中統三年為限，後是者不錄。

translations.literal: Selection standards should not be limited to Zhongtong 3; those after that date should not be excluded from registration.
translations.idiomatic: Selection criteria should not cut off at Zhongtong 3; candidates after that year should not be barred.

sentences.zh: 」帝是其言，敕中書施行。

translations.literal: " The emperor approved his words and ordered the Secretariat to implement them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved his advice and ordered the Secretariat to carry it out.

sentences.zh: 七年，遷益蘭州等五部斷事官，以比古之都護，治益蘭。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was transferred to be adjudication officer of Yilan and four other departments—equivalent to the Protector-General of antiquity—and governed Yilan.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was made adjudication officer of Yilan and four other departments, a post likened to the Protector-General of old, and governed from Yilan.

sentences.zh: 其地距京師九千餘里，民俗不知陶冶，水無舟航。

translations.literal: The place was more than nine thousand li from the capital; local customs had no knowledge of pottery and smelting, and the waters had no boats or navigation.
translations.idiomatic: The region lay more than nine thousand li from the capital; the people knew nothing of pottery or metalworking, and the rivers had no boats.

sentences.zh: 好禮請工匠於朝，以教其民，迄今稱便。

translations.literal: Haoli requested craftsmen from court to teach the people; to this day it is said to be convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Haoli requested craftsmen from court to teach the people, and the benefit is praised to this day.

sentences.zh: 或言榷鹽酒可以佐經費，好禮曰：「朝廷設官要荒，務以綏遠，寧欲奪其利耶！

translations.literal: Someone said that monopolizing salt and wine could supplement government expenses. Haoli said: "The court establishes officials in distant borderlands to pacify the far regions—would it really wish to seize their profits?"
translations.idiomatic: When someone proposed monopolizing salt and wine to supplement revenue, Haoli said, "The court posts officials in distant lands to pacify the frontier—would it truly mean to strip them of their livelihood?"

sentences.zh: 」言者慚服。

translations.literal: " The speaker felt ashamed and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: The proponent withdrew, ashamed and convinced.

sentences.zh: 十年，北方諸王叛，執好禮軍中，幾死，其大將以好禮善應對，釋之。

translations.literal: In the tenth year the northern princes rebelled; Haoli was seized in the army camp and nearly killed, but a senior commander released him because Haoli answered well.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year the northern princes rebelled. Haoli was taken in camp and nearly killed, but a senior commander spared him for his ready and tactful replies.

sentences.zh: 十六年春，叛王召好禮至欠欠州曰：「皇帝疑我，致有今日。

translations.literal: In the spring of the sixteenth year the rebel prince summoned Haoli to Qianqian Prefecture and said: "The emperor suspected me, which led to today."
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the sixteenth year the rebel prince summoned Haoli to Qianqian Prefecture and said, "The emperor's suspicion of me brought us to this pass."

sentences.zh: 」好禮曰：「不疑。

translations.literal: " Haoli said: "He did not suspect you."
translations.idiomatic: Haoli replied, "He did not suspect you."

sentences.zh: 果疑王，召王至京師，肯還之耶？

translations.literal: If he truly suspected you, would he summon you to the capital and then send you back?
translations.idiomatic: If he truly suspected you, would he summon you to the capital and then let you return?

sentences.zh: 」十七年春，好禮率眾走別部，守厄以待兵至。

translations.literal: " In the spring of the seventeenth year Haoli led his followers to flee to another tribe and held a strategic pass waiting for troops to arrive.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the seventeenth year Haoli led his followers to another tribe, held a mountain pass, and waited for imperial troops.

sentences.zh: 遇叛王軍，迫好禮西逾雪峨嶺。

translations.literal: They encountered the rebel prince's army, which forced Haoli west over Xue'e Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: They met the rebel prince's army, which drove Haoli west over Xue'e Ridge.

sentences.zh: 好禮自度，逾是則無望其還，遂以衣服賂叛王千戶，始獲東出鐵壁山口，間道南走數日，從者繼至且千人。

translations.literal: Haoli reckoned that once he passed that point there would be no hope of return, so he bribed a rebel prince's chiliarch with clothing and only then managed to go east out of Tiebi Mountain Pass; by hidden paths he fled south for several days, and followers continued to arrive until there were nearly a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Haoli judged that farther west there would be no hope of return. He bribed a rebel chiliarch with clothing and only then got free east through Tiebi Mountain Pass; by back trails he fled south for days while followers kept joining until he had nearly a thousand men.

sentences.zh: 中道糧絕，捕獵以為食。

translations.literal: Midway food ran out; they hunted for sustenance.
translations.idiomatic: Food gave out on the way, and they lived by hunting.

sentences.zh: 七月，至菊海，始與戍兵接，得乘傳至昌州。
