translations.literal: In the seventh month they reached Juhai and first made contact with garrison troops; he was able to take relays to Chang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month they reached Juhai, met garrison troops at last, and he traveled by relay post to Chang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 入見，帝賜之食與鈔。

translations.literal: He entered for an audience; the emperor bestowed food and paper money on him.
translations.idiomatic: He was received in audience, and the emperor gave him food and paper money.

sentences.zh: 十八年，授嘉議大夫、澧州路總管。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was granted Gentleman for Honorable Counsel and made route prefect of Lizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he was made Gentleman for Honorable Counsel and route prefect of Lizhou.

sentences.zh: 十九年，入為刑部尚書，俄改禮部，又改吏部。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he entered the capital as minister of punishments; soon he was changed to the Ministry of Rites, then again to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year he entered the capital as minister of punishments, then was moved to the Ministry of Rites and later to the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 好禮建言中書：「像力最巨，上往還兩都，乘輿象駕，萬一有變，從者雖多，力何能及。

translations.literal: Haoli memorialized the Secretariat: "Elephants have the greatest strength; when His Majesty travels between the two capitals riding in an elephant carriage, should anything go wrong, however many attendants there are, what strength could match it?"
translations.idiomatic: Haoli advised the Secretariat: "Elephants are immensely powerful. When His Majesty travels between the two capitals in an elephant carriage, if anything goes wrong, no number of attendants could restrain it."

sentences.zh: 」未幾，象驚，幾傷從者。

translations.literal: " Before long an elephant was startled and nearly injured attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Before long an elephant panicked and nearly injured attendants.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，出為北京路總管。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he went out as route prefect of the Northern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year he was posted as route prefect of the Northern Capital.

sentences.zh: 再入為戶部尚書。

translations.literal: He again entered as minister of revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to the capital as minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 二十五年六月，卒，年六十二。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the twenty-fifth year he died, at age sixty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the sixth month of the twenty-fifth year, at sixty-two.

sentences.zh: 子晸，為河西隴右道肅政廉訪使。

translations.literal: His son Jing served as rectifying surveillance commissioner of the Hexi Longyou Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jing became rectifying surveillance commissioner of the Hexi-Longyou Circuit.

sentences.zh: ○王國昌

translations.literal: Wang Guochang
translations.idiomatic: Wang Guochang

sentences.zh: 子燕出不花，襲武德將軍、左衛親軍副都指揮使。

translations.literal: His son Yanchubuhua inherited the rank of General of Martial Virtue and vice commander-in-chief of the Left Guard's personal army.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yanchubuhua inherited the posts of General of Martial Virtue and vice commander-in-chief of the Left Guard's personal army.

sentences.zh: ○姜彧

translations.literal: Jiang Yu
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Yu

sentences.zh: 姜彧，字文卿，萊州萊陽人也。

translations.literal: Jiang Yu, courtesy name Wenqing, was a man of Laiyang in Laizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Yu, courtesy name Wenqing, was from Laiyang in Laizhou.

sentences.zh: 父椿，避亂往依濟南張榮，因家焉。

translations.literal: His father Chun fled the chaos and went to rely on Zhang Rong of Jinan, and the family settled there.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chun fled the turmoil and took refuge with Zhang Rong of Jinan, and the family settled there.

sentences.zh: 彧幼穎悟好學，榮守濟南，辟為掾，升左右司知事，尋遷郎中，進參議官。

translations.literal: Yu was precocious and fond of learning; when Rong defended Jinan he recruited Yu as a clerk, promoted him to registrar of the left and right departments, soon transferred him to langzhong, and advanced him to deliberator.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was bright and studious from youth. When Rong held Jinan he recruited Yu as a clerk, then made him registrar of the left and right departments, soon promoted him to langzhong, and finally to deliberator.

sentences.zh: 中統二年，彧與榮孫宏入朝，因言益都李璮反狀已露，宜先其未發製之，未報。

translations.literal: In Zhongtong 2, Yu and Rong's grandson Hong went to court and reported that Li Tan of Yidu had already shown signs of rebellion and should be dealt with before he acted; there was no reply.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhongtong 2, Yu and Rong's grandson Hong went to court and warned that Li Tan of Yidu already showed clear signs of rebellion and should be stopped before he acted; no answer came.

sentences.zh: 明年春，璮果反。

translations.literal: The next spring Tan indeed rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: The next spring Tan did rebel.

sentences.zh: 時諸郡不為兵備，璮即襲據濟南。

translations.literal: At the time the various prefectures had made no military preparations, and Tan immediately seized Jinan by surprise attack.
translations.idiomatic: The prefectures had made no military preparations, and Tan seized Jinan at once.

sentences.zh: 彧棄家從榮，招集散亡。

translations.literal: Yu abandoned his family to follow Rong and gathered the scattered and displaced.
translations.idiomatic: Yu left his household to follow Rong and rallied the scattered and displaced.

sentences.zh: 迎諸王哈必赤進兵討之。

translations.literal: They welcomed Prince Habeichi to advance troops to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: They welcomed Prince Habeichi and his army to suppress the rebellion.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，捕得生口，言城中糧盡勢蹙，彧乃昏夜請見王曰：「聞王陛辭時，面受詔曰：'發兵誅璮耳，毋及無辜。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn they captured prisoners who said the city's grain was exhausted and its situation desperate; Yu then requested an audience with the prince at night and said: "I heard that when Your Highness took leave at court you received the edict in person: 'Send troops to execute Tan only; do not harm the innocent.'"
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month prisoners reported that the city was out of grain and hard pressed. Yu sought a night audience with the prince and said, "When Your Highness took leave at court, you were told in person: 'Send troops to punish Tan alone; do not touch the innocent.'"

sentences.zh: '今旦夕城且破，王宜早諭諸將分守城門，勿令縱兵，不然城中無噍類矣。

translations.literal: ' The city will fall at any moment; Your Highness should promptly instruct the generals to guard the gates separately and not allow troops to run loose, or else not one person will be left alive in the city.
translations.idiomatic: The city will fall at any moment. Your Highness should order the generals to hold the gates and forbid looting, or the whole population will be wiped out."

sentences.zh: 」王曰：「汝言城破，解陰陽耶？

translations.literal: " The prince said: "You say the city will fall—do you understand yin and yang?"
translations.idiomatic: The prince asked, "You say the city will fall—are you a diviner of yin and yang?"

sentences.zh: 」彧曰：「以人事知之，若待城破言於王，晚矣。

translations.literal: " Yu said: "I know it from human affairs; if I waited until the city fell to speak to Your Highness, it would be too late."
translations.idiomatic: Yu answered, "I infer it from the situation. If I waited until the city fell to tell Your Highness, it would be too late."

sentences.zh: 」王悟。

translations.literal: " The prince understood.
translations.idiomatic: The prince took his point.

sentences.zh: 明日，賊眾開門出降，王下令諸軍，敢入城者論以軍法，璮就擒，城中按堵如故。

translations.literal: The next day the rebel forces opened the gates and surrendered; the prince ordered the armies that anyone entering the city would be punished by military law; Tan was captured, and peace and order in the city remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the rebels opened the gates and surrendered. The prince ordered that anyone entering the city would be punished under military law. Tan was captured, and the city remained calm and intact.

sentences.zh: 彧以功授大都督府參議，改知濱州。

translations.literal: For his merit Yu was appointed deliberator of the Metropolitan Commandery Office and then made prefect of Binzhou.
translations.idiomatic: For his service Yu was made deliberator of the Metropolitan Commandery Office, then prefect of Binzhou.

sentences.zh: 時行營軍士多佔民田為牧地，縱牛馬壞民禾稼桑棗，彧言於中書，遣官分畫疆畔，捕其強猾不法者置之法。

translations.literal: At the time camp soldiers often seized commoners' fields as pasture and let oxen and horses ruin the people's grain, mulberry, and jujube; Yu reported to the Secretariat, which sent officials to demarcate boundaries and arrest the violent and lawless for punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Camp soldiers often seized civilian fields for pasture and let livestock ruin crops, mulberry, and jujube trees. Yu reported this to the Secretariat, which sent officials to mark boundaries and punish the worst offenders.

sentences.zh: 乃課民種桑，歲餘，新桑遍野，人名為太守桑。

translations.literal: He then assigned the people to plant mulberry; after a little more than a year new mulberry trees covered the countryside, and people called them the prefect's mulberry.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered the people to plant mulberry. Within a year new trees covered the countryside, and people called them the Prefect's Mulberry.

sentences.zh: 及遷東平府判官，民遮請留，馬為之不行。

translations.literal: When he was transferred to be assistant prefect of Dongping Prefecture, the people blocked the road asking him to stay, and the horses could not go forward.
translations.idiomatic: When he was transferred to assistant prefect of Dongping, the people blocked his path and begged him to stay; his horses would not move on.

sentences.zh: 至元五年，召拜治書侍御史，出為河北河南道提刑按察使，賜金虎符，改信州路總管。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhiyuan he was summoned and appointed investigating censor, then sent out as surveillance commissioner of the Hebei-Henan Circuit, granted a gold tiger tally, and changed to route prefect of Xinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiyuan 5 he was summoned as investigating censor, then posted as surveillance commissioner of the Hebei-Henan Circuit with a gold tiger tally, and later made route prefect of Xinzhou.

sentences.zh: 後累遷陝西漢中、河東山西道提刑按察使，拜行台御史中丞。

translations.literal: Later he was repeatedly transferred to be surveillance commissioner of the Shaanxi-Hanzhong and Hedong-Shanxi Circuits and appointed associate censor-in-chief of the Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He later served in turn as surveillance commissioner of the Shaanxi-Hanzhong and Hedong-Shanxi Circuits and was made associate censor-in-chief of the Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 後以老病歸濟南，尋擢燕南河北道提刑按察使。

translations.literal: Later, because of age and illness he returned to Jinan; soon he was promoted to surveillance commissioner of the Yannan-Hebei Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He later retired to Jinan with age and illness, but was soon promoted to surveillance commissioner of the Yannan-Hebei Circuit.

sentences.zh: 三十年二月，以疾卒，年七十六。

translations.literal: In the second month of the thirtieth year he died of illness, at age seventy-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died of illness in the second month of the thirtieth year, at seventy-six.

sentences.zh: 子迪吉。

translations.literal: His son was Diji.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Diji.

sentences.zh: ○張礎

translations.literal: Zhang Chu
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chu

sentences.zh: 張礎，字可用，其先渤海人，金末，曾祖琛徙燕之通州。

translations.literal: Zhang Chu, courtesy name Keyong, his ancestors were men of Bohai; at the end of Jin his great-grandfather Chen moved to Tongzhou in Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chu, courtesy name Keyong, came from Bohai stock; at the end of Jin his great-grandfather Chen moved the family to Tongzhou in Yan.

sentences.zh: 祖伯達，從忽都忽那顏略地燕、薊，金守蒲察七斤以城降。

translations.literal: His grandfather Boda followed Commander Huduhu in reducing the lands of Yan and Ji; the Jin defender Pucha Qijin surrendered the city.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Boda followed Commander Huduhu in the conquest of Yan and Ji; the Jin defender Pucha Qijin surrendered the city.

sentences.zh: 忽都忽承製以伯達為通州節度判官，遂知通州。

translations.literal: Huduhu, acting on imperial authority, appointed Boda military adjutant of Tongzhou and he then governed Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Huduhu appointed Boda military adjutant of Tongzhou on imperial authority, and Boda went on to govern the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父範，為真定勸農官，因家焉。

translations.literal: His father Fan served as agricultural promotion officer of Zhending, and the family settled there.
translations.idiomatic: His father Fan served as agricultural promotion officer of Zhending, and the family settled there.

sentences.zh: 礎業儒，丙辰歲，平章廉希憲薦於世祖潛邸。

translations.literal: Chu pursued Confucian studies; in the bingchen year Grand Councillor Lian Xixian recommended him to the Heir Apparent Kublai's residence.
translations.idiomatic: Chu studied the Confucian classics; in the bingchen year Grand Councillor Lian Xixian recommended him to Kublai's princely residence.

sentences.zh: 時真定為諸王阿里不哥分地，阿里不哥以礎不附己，銜之，遣使言於世祖曰：「張礎，我分地中人，當以歸我。

translations.literal: At the time Zhending was the appanage of Prince Ariq Böke; because Chu did not attach himself to him, Ariq Böke resented him and sent a messenger to tell Kublai: "Zhang Chu is a man of my appanage and should be returned to me."
translations.idiomatic: Zhending then lay in Prince Ariq Böke's appanage. Because Chu would not side with him, Ariq Böke resented him and sent word to Kublai: "Zhang Chu belongs to my domain and should be returned to me."

sentences.zh: 」世祖命使者復曰：「兄弟至親，寧有彼此之間，且我方有事於宋，如礎者，實所倚任，待天下平定，當遣還也。

translations.literal: " Kublai ordered the messenger to reply: "Brothers are closest kin—how could there be a divide between us? Moreover I now have business with Song, and men like Chu are ones I truly rely on; when the realm is pacified I shall send him back."
translations.idiomatic: Kublai had the envoy reply, "Brothers are closest of kin—why speak of yours and mine? I have urgent business with Song, and men like Chu are indispensable to me. When the realm is settled I will send him back."

sentences.zh: 」己未，從世祖伐宋，凡徵發軍旅文檄，悉出其手。

translations.literal: " In the jiwei year he followed Kublai in attacking Song; all military requisition documents and proclamations came from his hand.
translations.idiomatic: In the jiwei year he followed Kublai's campaign against Song and drafted all military requisitions and proclamations.

sentences.zh: 中統元年，立中書省，以礎權左右司事，尋出為彰德路拘榷官，復入為三部員外郎，賜金符，為平陽路同知轉運使，改知獻州，同知東平府事，又改知威州。

translations.literal: In Zhongtong 1 the Secretariat was established; Chu was put in charge of the left and right departments, soon sent out as monopoly officer of Zhangde Route, then re-entered as outer section director of the three ministries, granted a gold tally, made associate transport commissioner of Pingyang Route, changed to prefect of Xianzhou, associate prefect of Dongping Prefecture, and again changed to prefect of Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhongtong 1, when the Secretariat was established, Chu temporarily headed the left and right departments. He then served as monopoly officer of Zhangde Route, returned as outer section director of the three ministries with a gold tally, became associate transport commissioner of Pingyang Route, prefect of Xianzhou, associate prefect of Dongping, and finally prefect of Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 有婦人乘驢過市者，投下官暗赤之奴引鳴鏑射婦人墜地，奴匿暗赤家。

translations.literal: A woman riding a donkey passed through the market; a slave of the appanage official Anchi shot a whistling arrow and knocked the woman to the ground; the slave hid in Anchi's house.
translations.idiomatic: A woman riding a donkey passed through the market. A slave of the appanage official Anchi shot a whistling arrow and knocked her to the ground, then hid in Anchi's house.

sentences.zh: 礎將以其事聞，暗赤懼，乃出其奴，論如法。

translations.literal: Chu was about to report the matter; Anchi feared this and produced the slave, who was punished according to law.
translations.idiomatic: When Chu was about to report the case, Anchi, fearing exposure, surrendered the slave, who was punished by law.

sentences.zh: 至元十四年，立諸道提刑按察司，以礎為江南浙西道提刑按察副使，佩金符。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Zhiyuan the circuit surveillance commissions were established; Chu was made associate surveillance commissioner of the Jiangnan-Zhexi Circuit and wore a gold tally.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiyuan 14, when circuit surveillance commissions were established, Chu became associate surveillance commissioner of the Jiangnan-Zhexi Circuit with a gold tally.

sentences.zh: 宣慰使失裡貪暴，掠良民為奴，礎劾黜之。

translations.literal: Pacification Commissioner Shili was greedy and violent, seizing good commoners as slaves; Chu impeached and removed him.
translations.idiomatic: Pacification Commissioner Shili was greedy and brutal and seized commoners as slaves; Chu impeached him and had him removed.

sentences.zh: 遂安縣民聚眾負險為亂，命礎與同知浙西道宣慰使劉宣領兵捕之。

translations.literal: Commoners of Suian County gathered in numbers, relying on rugged terrain to rebel; Chu was ordered together with Associate Pacification Commissioner Liu Xuan of the Zhexi Circuit to lead troops to capture them.
translations.idiomatic: People in Suian County rose in armed rebellion from rugged terrain. Chu and Associate Pacification Commissioner Liu Xuan of the Zhexi Circuit were ordered to lead troops against them.

sentences.zh: 宣即欲進兵，礎曰：「江南新附，守吏或失撫字，宜遣人招諭，以全眾命。

translations.literal: Xuan at once wished to advance the army; Chu said: "Jiangnan has only recently submitted; local officials may have failed in care and governance—messengers should be sent to summon them by edict and preserve the lives of the multitude."
translations.idiomatic: Xuan wanted to attack at once. Chu said, "Jiangnan has only just submitted; local officials may have failed the people. Send envoys to offer terms and save lives."

sentences.zh: 」宣不可，礎曰：「諭之不來，加誅未晚。

translations.literal: " Xuan would not agree; Chu said: "If summoning them fails, punishment will not be too late."
translations.idiomatic: Xuan refused. Chu said, "If they ignore the summons, punishment can come later."

sentences.zh: 」遂遣人諭之，逆黨果自縛請罪，礎釋之，宣乃嘆服。

translations.literal: " Envoys were then sent to summon them; the rebels indeed bound themselves and asked forgiveness; Chu released them, and Xuan then sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys were sent. The rebels bound themselves and pleaded for mercy; Chu released them, and Xuan came away impressed.

sentences.zh: 遷嶺南廣西道提刑按察使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be surveillance commissioner of the Lingnan-Guangxi Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to surveillance commissioner of the Lingnan-Guangxi Circuit.

sentences.zh: 廣西宣慰使也裡脫強奪民財，礎按其罪。

translations.literal: Guangxi Pacification Commissioner Yelituo forcibly seized commoners' property; Chu investigated and charged him with the crime.
translations.idiomatic: Guangxi Pacification Commissioner Yelituo seized civilian property by force; Chu investigated and prosecuted him.

sentences.zh: 遷嶺北湖南道提刑按察副使，授賓州路總管，不赴，拜國子祭酒，尋出為安豐路總管。

translations.literal: He was transferred to associate surveillance commissioner of the Lingbei-Hunan Circuit, appointed route prefect of Binzhou but did not take up the post, was appointed director of the Imperial Academy, and soon went out as route prefect of Anfeng.
translations.idiomatic: He was made associate surveillance commissioner of the Lingbei-Hunan Circuit, offered the post of route prefect of Binzhou but declined, was appointed director of the Imperial Academy, and soon became route prefect of Anfeng.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，卒於官，年六十三。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year he died in office, at age sixty-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office in the thirty-first year, at sixty-three.

sentences.zh: 贈昭文館大學士、正奉大夫，封清河郡公，諡文敏。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Grand Academician of the Zhaowen Hall and Grand Master for Proper Service, enfeoffed as Duke of Qinghe Commandery, with the posthumous title Wenmin.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Grand Academician of the Zhaowen Hall and Grand Master for Proper Service, enfeoffed as Duke of Qinghe Commandery, with the posthumous name Wenmin.

sentences.zh: 子淑，衛輝路推官。

translations.literal: His son Shu served as judicial officer of Weihui Route.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shu served as judicial officer of Weihui Route.

sentences.zh: ○呂掞

translations.literal: Lu Shan
translations.idiomatic: Lu Shan

sentences.zh: 呂掞字，伯充，河內人。

translations.literal: Lu Shan, courtesy name Bochong, was a man of Henei.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Shan, courtesy name Bochong, was from Henei.

sentences.zh: 七世祖公緒，與宋丞相公著為從昆弟。

translations.literal: His seventh-generation ancestor Gongxu was a paternal cousin of Song Chancellor Gongzhu.
translations.idiomatic: His seventh-generation ancestor Gongxu was a paternal cousin of the Song chancellor Lu Gongzhu.

sentences.zh: 祖庭，金末避亂，去鄉里。

translations.literal: His grandfather Ting, at the end of Jin fleeing chaos, left his native place.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Ting left his home at the end of Jin to escape the turmoil.

sentences.zh: 父佑，歸附，初隸兵籍，轉徙北郡，復至關中，家焉。

translations.literal: His father You submitted to the new dynasty; at first enrolled in the military registers, he moved among northern commanderies, then returned to Guanzhong and settled there.
translations.idiomatic: His father You submitted to the new regime, was first enrolled in the military registers, moved through the northern commanderies, and finally settled in Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 廉希憲宣撫京兆，聘許衡教授生徒，掞從衡學。

translations.literal: Lian Xixian pacified Jingzhao and engaged Xu Heng to instruct students; Shan studied under Heng.
translations.idiomatic: When Lian Xixian pacified Jingzhao he engaged Xu Heng to teach students, and Shan studied under Xu Heng.

sentences.zh: 衡為國子祭酒，舉掞為伴讀，輔成教養，掞之功為多。

translations.literal: When Heng became director of the Imperial Academy he recommended Shan as associate reader; in assisting the cultivation and education of students Shan's contribution was great.
translations.idiomatic: When Xu Heng became director of the Imperial Academy he recommended Shan as associate reader; Shan did much to help train the students.

sentences.zh: 至元十三年，擢陝西道按察司知事。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Zhiyuan he was promoted to registrar of the Shaanxi Circuit Surveillance Commission.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiyuan 13 he was promoted to registrar of the Shaanxi Circuit Surveillance Commission.

sentences.zh: 未行，會宋降者言襄、漢新附，民情未安，有呂子開者，向為襄陽制置司參謀官，今退居鄂，其人悉知宋事，宜徵用之，朝廷議遣使而難其人。

translations.literal: Before he departed, a Song surrenderer reported that Xiang and Han had newly submitted and the people's hearts were not yet settled; there was a man named Lu Zikai who had formerly been staff officer of the Xiangyang Pacification Commission and now lived in retirement at E—he thoroughly knew Song affairs and should be summoned to serve; the court discussed sending an envoy but found it hard to choose the man.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could take up the post, a Song surrenderer reported that the newly submitted Xiang-Han region was still unsettled. A man named Lu Zikai, formerly staff officer of the Xiangyang Pacification Commission and now retired in E, knew Song affairs thoroughly and should be recruited. The court debated whom to send as envoy.

sentences.zh: 或言子開舊名偉，金亂入宋，更名文蔚，字子開，於掞為從叔父，宜遣掞行。

translations.literal: Someone said Zikai's original name was Wei; during Jin chaos he entered Song and changed his name to Wenwei, courtesy name Zikai—he was Shan's father's younger cousin—and Shan should be sent.
translations.idiomatic: Someone noted that Zikai's original name was Wei; he had entered Song during the Jin collapse and renamed himself Wenwei, styled Zikai. As Shan's grand-uncle, Shan was the right envoy.

sentences.zh: 時江淮兵猶未戢，掞聞之，慨然請行。

translations.literal: At the time fighting along the Jiang and Huai had not yet ceased; when Shan heard this he resolutely volunteered to go.
translations.idiomatic: Fighting along the Jiang-Huai had not yet ended, but when Shan heard of the mission he volunteered at once.

sentences.zh: 子開既入覲，陳安撫襄、漢便宜，詔以子開為翰林直學士，辭不就。

translations.literal: After Zikai entered for an audience he set forth convenient measures for pacifying Xiang and Han; an edict appointed Zikai Hanlin Academician, but he declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: After Zikai was received at court he proposed measures to pacify the Xiang-Han region. The court appointed him Hanlin Academician, but he declined.

sentences.zh: 十四年，授掞四川行樞密院都事。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year Shan was appointed chief clerk of the Sichuan Branch Privy Council.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year Shan was made chief clerk of the Sichuan Branch Privy Council.

sentences.zh: 時宋制置使張珏守重慶，安撫使王立守合州，詔樞府分兵取之。

translations.literal: At the time Song Pacification Commissioner Zhang Jue defended Chongqing and Pacification Commissioner Wang Li defended Hezhou; an edict ordered the Privy Council to divide troops and take them.
translations.idiomatic: Song Pacification Commissioner Zhang Jue held Chongqing and Pacification Commissioner Wang Li held Hezhou. The Privy Council was ordered to divide forces and take both.

sentences.zh: 李德輝行西院事於成都，獲立偵卒張郃等數人，將殺之，掞曰：「彼不即降者，以昔嘗抗命，城降懼誅耳。

translations.literal: Li Dehui acted for the Western Branch at Chengdu and captured several of Wang Li's scouts including Zhang He; he was about to kill them. Shan said: "Those who do not surrender at once do so because they once resisted orders and fear execution after the city submits."
translations.idiomatic: Li Dehui, acting head of the Western Branch at Chengdu, captured several of Wang Li's scouts, including Zhang He, and was about to execute them. Shan said, "They hold out because they once resisted and fear death even if the city falls."

sentences.zh: 今宜釋郃等，俾歸諭立。

translations.literal: Now Zhang He and the others should be released and sent back to persuade Wang Li.
translations.idiomatic: Release Zhang He and the others now and send them back to persuade Wang Li.

sentences.zh: 」未幾，立果遣郃等齎蠟書至成都，德輝請與東院同受降。

translations.literal: " Before long Wang Li indeed sent Zhang He and the others bearing a wax-sealed letter to Chengdu; Dehui requested to receive the surrender together with the Eastern Branch.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Wang Li sent Zhang He and the others to Chengdu with a wax-sealed letter of surrender. Dehui asked to accept the surrender jointly with the Eastern Branch.

sentences.zh: 後期不至，德輝承製授立仍為安撫使，知合州，開倉賑民，禁戢剽掠。

translations.literal: When the appointed deadline passed without the Eastern Branch arriving, Dehui, acting on imperial authority, appointed Wang Li again as pacification commissioner and prefect of Hezhou, opened granaries to relieve the people, and forbade plunder.
translations.idiomatic: When the Eastern Branch failed to arrive by the agreed time, Dehui, acting on imperial authority, reappointed Wang Li pacification commissioner and prefect of Hezhou, opened granaries to feed the people, and forbade looting.

sentences.zh: 而瀘、敘、崇慶、播、夔、萬等郡聞之，相繼送款。

translations.literal: And the prefectures of Lu, Xu, Chongqing, Bo, Kui, Wan, and others, hearing of it, submitted in succession.
translations.idiomatic: When Luzhou, Xuzhou, Chongqing, Bozhou, Kuizhou, Wanzhou, and other prefectures heard of it, they submitted one after another.

sentences.zh: 巴、黔民感掞與德輝之惠，並祠事之。

translations.literal: The people of Ba and Qian, grateful for the benefits from Shan and Dehui, both enshrined and worshipped them.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Ba and Qian, grateful for the kindness shown them by Shan and Dehui, enshrined and worshipped them both.

sentences.zh: 東院恥其無功，誣德輝越境邀功，械立於長安獄，將誅之。

translations.literal: The Eastern Branch, shamed at its lack of achievement, falsely accused Dehui of crossing borders to claim credit, put him in shackles in the Chang'an prison, and intended to execute him.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Branch, ashamed that it had accomplished nothing, falsely accused Dehui of crossing jurisdictional boundaries to steal credit, shackled him, and imprisoned him in Chang'an, intending to put him to death.

sentences.zh: 掞適以事至京師，言於許衡。

translations.literal: Shan happened to be in the capital on business and spoke to Xu Heng.
translations.idiomatic: Shan happened to be in the capital on business and told Xu Heng what had happened.

sentences.zh: 衡白留守賀仁傑，遂奏釋立，賜金虎符，仍舊官。

translations.literal: Heng informed the acting governor He Renjie, who then memorialized for Dehui's release, granted a gold tiger tally, and restored him to his former office.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Heng informed the acting governor He Renjie, who memorialized for Dehui's release. Dehui was freed, granted a gold tiger tally, and restored to his former post.

sentences.zh: 掞亦以平定四川功，詔賜金織衣、弓刀、鞍勒、白金，升奉訓大夫、四川行省左右司郎中。

translations.literal: Shan also, for merit in pacifying Sichuan, was by edict granted a gold brocade robe, bow and blade, saddle and bridle, and white silver, and promoted to Grand Master for Fostering Instruction and director of the left and right bureaus of the Sichuan Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: For his part in pacifying Sichuan, Shan was granted by edict a gold brocade robe, bow and blade, saddle and bridle, and white silver, and was promoted to Grand Master for Fostering Instruction and director of the left and right bureaus of the Sichuan Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 十九年，調同知順慶路總管府事，以疾辭。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he was transferred to be associate administrator of the Shunqing Route Directorate, but declined on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year he was appointed associate administrator of the Shunqing Route Directorate but declined because of illness.

sentences.zh: 二十年，徵為國子司業，以未終喪辭。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he was summoned as vice director of the Directorate of the Imperial Academy but declined because his mourning period was unfinished.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year he was summoned to serve as vice director of the Directorate of the Imperial Academy but declined because he had not yet completed mourning.

sentences.zh: 三十年，改華州知州，勸農興學，具有成效，及代，民爭留之。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year he was reassigned as prefect of Huazhou; he encouraged farming and promoted learning with marked success, and when his term ended the people struggled to keep him.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year he was made prefect of Huazhou. He encouraged agriculture and promoted learning with clear success, and when his term ended the people competed to keep him.

sentences.zh: 子三人：杲、果、楨，皆顯仕。

translations.literal: He had three sons: Gao, Guo, and Zhen—all rose to prominent office.
translations.idiomatic: He had three sons—Gao, Guo, and Zhen—all of whom rose to distinguished office.

sentences.zh: 孫魯，濟寧路總管。

translations.literal: His grandson Lu was administrator of Jining Route.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Lu served as administrator of Jining Route.

sentences.zh: ○譚資榮

translations.literal: Tan Zirong
translations.idiomatic: Tan Zirong

sentences.zh: 譚資榮，字茂卿，德興懷來人。

translations.literal: Tan Zirong, courtesy name Maoqing, was a man of Huailai in Dexing.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Zirong, courtesy name Maoqing, was from Huailai in Dexing.

sentences.zh: 敦厚寡言，頗知讀書，仕金為縣令。

translations.literal: Steadfast and taciturn, he was well read; under Jin he served as county magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: Steadfast and sparing of speech, he was well read and served the Jin as county magistrate.

sentences.zh: 歲己卯，河朔歸版圖，資榮率眾款附，主帥稔聞其名，即日以金符授元帥左都監，為縣令如故。

translations.literal: In the jimao year, when the Hebei north submitted to the realm, Zirong led the people in surrendering; the commander, having long heard his name, that same day granted him a gold tally as left chief overseer of the Marshal's Office, continuing as county magistrate as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the jimao year, when the north of the Yellow River came under the dynasty's rule, Zirong led his people in submitting. The commander, who had long known his reputation, that very day granted him a gold tally and made him left chief overseer of the Marshal's Office while keeping him county magistrate as before.

sentences.zh: 後從征，以功賜金虎符，升行元帥府事，復以其弟資用代充元帥左監軍。

translations.literal: Later he followed on campaign; for merit he was granted a gold tiger tally and promoted to deputy marshal's headquarters, and his younger brother Ziyong was appointed in his stead as left army overseer of the Marshal's Office.
translations.idiomatic: He later followed on campaign and, for his merit, was granted a gold tiger tally and promoted to deputy head of the Marshal's Headquarters. His younger brother Ziyong replaced him as left army overseer of the Marshal's Office.

sentences.zh: 歲壬辰，資榮從攻汴梁有功。

translations.literal: In the renchen year Zirong followed the attack on Bianliang with merit.
translations.idiomatic: In the renchen year Zirong took part in the assault on Bianliang and distinguished himself.

sentences.zh: 既而舉資用自代，退而耕田讀書，以為逸老計，時年四十。

translations.literal: Thereafter he recommended Ziyong to replace him, retired to farm and read books as a plan for leisurely old age—he was then forty.
translations.idiomatic: He then recommended Ziyong to succeed him, retired to farm and read, and made that his plan for a peaceful old age. He was forty at the time.

sentences.zh: 子二人：曰澄，曰山阜。

translations.literal: He had two sons: Cheng and Shanfu.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons, Cheng and Shanfu.

sentences.zh: 澄好讀書，又習國語，為監縣，多善政。

translations.literal: Cheng loved reading and also studied the national language; as supervising magistrate he had many good policies.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng loved books and also studied the national language. As supervising magistrate he carried out many good policies.

sentences.zh: 世祖在潛邸時，澄入見，世祖嘉其容止安詳，留居籓府，稱其官而不名，以其弟山阜代為縣。

translations.literal: When Kublai was still in his princely residence Cheng came to audience; the Prince admired his calm bearing and kept him at the residence, calling him by his office rather than his name, and had his younger brother Shanfu replace him as county magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: While Kublai was still in his princely residence, Cheng came to audience. The Prince admired his calm and dignified bearing, kept him at the residence, addressed him by his office rather than his name, and had his younger brother Shanfu take over the county post.

sentences.zh: 遣邇臣出使，必以澄偕。

translations.literal: Whenever close ministers were sent as envoys, Cheng was always sent along with them.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever close attendants were dispatched as envoys, Cheng was always sent with them.

sentences.zh: 中統元年，制書褒美，以為懷孟路總管。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhongtong an imperial letter praised him and appointed him administrator of Huaimeng Route.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhongtong 1 an imperial letter commended him and appointed him administrator of Huaimeng Route.

sentences.zh: 明年，入覲，賜金符。

translations.literal: The following year he attended court and was granted a gold tally.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he came to court and was granted a gold tally.

sentences.zh: 四年，易虎符。

translations.literal: In the fourth year his tiger tally was renewed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year his tiger tally was renewed.

sentences.zh: 居官時，訟至立決，教民力田務本。

translations.literal: In office he settled lawsuits on the spot and taught the people to work the fields and keep to fundamentals.
translations.idiomatic: In office he decided lawsuits as soon as they arrived and taught the people to work the land and attend to the root of livelihood.

sentences.zh: 歷彰德同知，遷河南路總管，兼府尹。

translations.literal: He served in turn as associate prefect of Zhangde and was transferred to administrator of Henan Route, concurrently prefect.
translations.idiomatic: He served as associate prefect of Zhangde, then was transferred to administrator of Henan Route and concurrently served as prefect.

sentences.zh: 明年，奔父喪。

translations.literal: The next year he hurried home for his father's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he rushed home upon his father's death.

sentences.zh: 中書不聽其終制，奏起復蒞職。

translations.literal: The Central Secretariat would not allow him to complete mourning and memorialized to recall him to office.
translations.idiomatic: The Central Secretariat would not let him complete mourning and memorialized to recall him to duty.

sentences.zh: 後歷司農少卿，遷陝西四川提刑按察使。

translations.literal: He later served as vice minister of the Directorate of Agriculture and was transferred to surveillance commissioner of the Shaanxi-Sichuan Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as vice minister of the Directorate of Agriculture and was transferred to surveillance commissioner of the Shaanxi-Sichuan Circuit.

sentences.zh: 逾年，西南夷羅羅斯內附，帝以澄文武兼資，可使鎮撫新國，以為副都元帥、同知宣慰使司事。

translations.literal: After a year the southwestern Yi of Luoluo submitted; the Emperor considered Cheng endowed with both civil and military capacity fit to pacify the new territory, and appointed him vice grand marshal and associate commissioner of the Pacification Commission.
translations.idiomatic: A year later the southwestern Yi of Luoluo submitted. The Emperor judged Cheng capable in both civil and military affairs and fit to pacify the newly submitted territory, and appointed him vice grand marshal and associate commissioner of the Pacification Commission.

sentences.zh: 至其境，諭之曰：「皇元一視同仁，不間遠近，特置大帥，安集招懷，以捍外侮，非利徵求於汝也。

translations.literal: On reaching the territory he admonished them, saying: "The Great Yuan treats all alike without distinction of near and far. A grand marshal is specially appointed to settle and win people over and repel external aggression—it is not to levy exactions upon you.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached the territory he addressed them: "The Great Yuan treats all with equal kindness, without regard to distance. A grand marshal has been specially appointed to settle the people, win their hearts, and repel outside aggression—not to profit by levying exactions on you.

sentences.zh: 」夷人大悅。

translations.literal: " The Yi were greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The Yi were greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 尋以疾卒。

translations.literal: Soon thereafter he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he died of illness.

sentences.zh: 子克修，事裕宗於東宮，出為江南湖北、河北河南、陝西漢中三道提刑按察使。

translations.literal: His son Kexiu served Prince Zhenjin in the Eastern Palace and later became surveillance commissioner of the Jiangnan-Hubei, Hebei-Henan, and Shaanxi-Hanzhong circuits.
translations.idiomatic: His son Kexiu served Prince Zhenjin in the Eastern Palace and later became surveillance commissioner of the Jiangnan-Hubei, Hebei-Henan, and Shaanxi-Hanzhong circuits.

sentences.zh: 孫男三人：曰忠，曰質，曰文。

translations.literal: He had three grandsons: Zhong, Zhi, and Wen.
translations.idiomatic: He had three grandsons: Zhong, Zhi, and Wen.

sentences.zh: ○王惲

translations.literal: Wang Yun
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yun

sentences.zh: 至元五年，建御史臺，首拜監察御史，知無不言，論列凡百五十餘章。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhiyuan, when the Censorate was established, Yun was first appointed investigating censor; he spoke without holding back and submitted more than a hundred and fifty memorials in all.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiyuan 5, when the Censorate was established, Yun was among the first appointed investigating censors. He held nothing back and submitted more than a hundred and fifty memorials in all.

sentences.zh: 時都水劉晸交結權勢，任用頗專，陷沒官糧四十餘萬石，惲劾之，暴其奸利，權貴側目。

translations.literal: At the time Liu Kan, director of waterways, colluded with powerful men and exercised his authority quite arbitrarily, embezzling more than four hundred thousand shi of government grain. Yun impeached him and exposed his corrupt profit-making; the powerful fixed him with hostile eyes.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Liu Kan, director of waterways, colluded with the powerful and wielded his authority with little restraint, embezzling more than four hundred thousand shi of government grain. Yun impeached him and exposed his corrupt profiteering, and the great families watched him with hostile eyes.

sentences.zh: 又言：「晸監修太廟畢功，特轉官錫賞，今才數年，梁柱摧朽，事涉不敬，宜論如法。

translations.literal: He also said: "When Kan supervised repairs to the Imperial Temple and the work was completed, he was specially promoted and rewarded. Now only a few years have passed and the beams and pillars are rotting and collapsing—the matter involves disrespect and he should be judged according to law.
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "When Kan supervised repairs to the Imperial Temple and the work was finished, he was specially promoted and rewarded. Yet only a few years later the beams and pillars are rotting away—a matter involving disrespect for which he should be judged according to law.

sentences.zh: 」晸竟以憂卒。

translations.literal: " Kan ultimately died of grief.
translations.idiomatic: Kan eventually died of grief.

sentences.zh: 秩滿，陳天祐、雷膺交薦於朝。

translations.literal: When his term expired, Chen Tianyou and Lei Ying jointly recommended him at court.
translations.idiomatic: When his term expired, Chen Tianyou and Lei Ying jointly recommended him to the court.

sentences.zh: 九年，授承​​直郎、平陽路總管府判官。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was appointed Gentleman for Attending Service and judge of the Pingyang Route Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was appointed Gentleman for Attending Service and judge of the Pingyang Route Directorate.

sentences.zh: 初，絳之太平縣民有陳氏者殺其兄，行賂緩獄，蔓引逮系者三百餘人，至五年不決。

translations.literal: Earlier, in Taiping County of Jiang, a man surnamed Chen killed his elder brother; by bribery he delayed the trial, and the case dragged on with more than three hundred persons implicated and detained, unresolved for five years.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in Taiping County in Jiang, a man surnamed Chen had killed his elder brother. By bribery he stalled the case, and more than three hundred people were implicated and detained; after five years it was still unresolved.

sentences.zh: 朝廷委惲鞫之，一訊即得其實，乃盡出所逮系者。

translations.literal: The court assigned Yun to examine the case; one interrogation yielded the truth, and he released all those detained.
translations.idiomatic: The court entrusted the case to Yun. One interrogation brought out the truth, and he released all those who had been detained.

sentences.zh: 時絳久旱，一夕大雨。

translations.literal: At the time Jiang had long suffered drought; one night a great rain fell.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang had long been in drought; that night a heavy rain fell.

sentences.zh: 十三年，奉命試儒人於河南。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was ordered to examine scholars in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he was ordered to examine Confucian scholars in Henan.

sentences.zh: 十四年，除翰林待制，拜朝列大夫、河南北道提刑按察副使，尋改置諸道製下，遷燕南河北道，按部諸郡，贓吏多所罷黜。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was made Hanlin academician-in-waiting and Court Gentleman for Attendance, vice surveillance commissioner of the Henan North Circuit; soon, when the various circuits were reorganized, he was transferred to the Yannan-Hebei Circuit; touring the commanderies he removed many corrupt officials.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he was made Hanlin academician-in-waiting and Court Gentleman for Attendance, vice surveillance commissioner of the Henan North Circuit. When the circuit offices were soon reorganized, he was transferred to the Yannan-Hebei Circuit; touring the commanderies, he dismissed many corrupt officials.

sentences.zh: 十八年，拜中議大夫、行御史臺治書侍御史，不赴。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was appointed Gentleman for Extended Governance and investigating secretary of the Branch Censorate but did not take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he was appointed Gentleman for Extended Governance and investigating secretary of the Branch Censorate, but he did not go.

sentences.zh: 裕宗在東宮，惲進《承華事略》，其目曰廣孝、立愛、端本、進學、擇術、謹習、聽政、達聰、撫軍、崇儒、親賢、去邪、納誨、幾諫、從諫、推恩、尚儉、戒逸、知賢、審官，凡二十篇。

translations.literal: When Prince Zhenjin was in the Eastern Palace, Yun presented the "Outline of Eastern Palace Affairs," with chapters titled Expanding Filial Piety, Establishing Love, Setting the Root Correct, Advancing Learning, Choosing Methods, Practicing with Care, Hearing Government, Reaching the Far, Pacifying the Army, Honoring Confucianism, Esteeming Worthies, Removing the Devious, Accepting Remonstrance, Subtle Remonstrance, Following Remonstrance, Extending Grace, Valuing Frugality, Guarding against Indulgence, Knowing Worthies, and Examining Officeholders—twenty sections in all.
translations.idiomatic: While Prince Zhenjin was in the Eastern Palace, Yun presented the Outline of Eastern Palace Affairs. Its chapters were Expanding Filial Piety, Establishing Love, Setting the Root Upright, Advancing Learning, Choosing Methods, Practicing with Care, Hearing Government, Reaching the Far, Pacifying the Army, Honoring Confucianism, Esteeming Worthies, Removing the Devious, Accepting Remonstrance, Subtle Remonstrance, Following Remonstrance, Extending Grace, Valuing Frugality, Guarding against Indulgence, Knowing Worthies, and Examining Officeholders—twenty sections in all.

sentences.zh: 裕宗覽之，至漢成帝不絕馳道，唐肅宗改服絳紗為硃明服，心甚喜，曰：「我若遇是禮，亦當如是。

translations.literal: When the Prince read it, upon reaching the passage about Emperor Cheng of Han not blocking the imperial thoroughfare and Emperor Suzong of Tang changing his red gauze robe to the Zhuming robe, his heart was greatly pleased, and he said: "If I encounter such rites, I too shall act in the same way.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince read it, he came to the passage about Emperor Cheng of Han not blocking the imperial thoroughfare and Emperor Suzong of Tang changing his red gauze robe to the Zhuming robe. His heart was greatly pleased, and he said, "If I meet with such rites, I too shall act in the same way.

sentences.zh: 」又至邢峙止齊太子食邪蒿，顧侍臣曰：「一菜之名，遽能邪人耶？

translations.literal: " Reading further to Xing Zhi's stopping the Qi crown prince from eating wild artemisia, he turned to his attendants and said: "Can the name of one vegetable so quickly lead a man astray?
translations.idiomatic: Reading further, he came to Xing Zhi's stopping the Qi crown prince from eating wild artemisia. He turned to his attendants and said, "Can the name of one vegetable really lead a man astray so quickly?

sentences.zh: 」詹事丞張九思從旁對曰：「正臣防微，理固當然。

translations.literal: " Chief steward Zhang Jiusi answered from the side: "Upright ministers guard against the slightest deviation—that is perfectly as it should be.
translations.idiomatic: Chief steward Zhang Jiusi answered from the side, "Upright ministers guard against the slightest lapse—that is only as it should be.

sentences.zh: 」太子善其說，賜酒慰喻之。

translations.literal: " The Prince approved his point and bestowed wine to comfort and praise him.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince approved his point and bestowed wine to comfort and praise him.

sentences.zh: 令諸皇孫傳觀，稱其書弘益居多。

translations.literal: He ordered all the imperial grandsons to pass the book around, saying it was largely of broad benefit.
translations.idiomatic: He had all the imperial grandsons pass the book around and praised it as being largely of broad benefit.

sentences.zh: 十九年春，改山東西道提刑按察副使，在官一年，以疾還衛。

translations.literal: In the spring of the nineteenth year he was reassigned vice surveillance commissioner of the Shandong East-West Circuit; after a year in office he returned home on account of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the nineteenth year he was made vice surveillance commissioner of the Shandong East-West Circuit. After a year in office he returned home because of illness.

sentences.zh: 二十二年春，以左司郎中召。

translations.literal: In the spring of the twenty-second year he was summoned as director of the left bureau.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the twenty-second year he was summoned to serve as director of the left bureau.

sentences.zh: 時右丞盧世榮以聚斂進用，屢趣之不赴。

translations.literal: At the time Right Chancellor Lu Shirong had risen through ruthless exactions and repeatedly urged him, but Yun would not go.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Right Chancellor Lu Shirong had risen through ruthless exactions and repeatedly pressed him, but Yun refused to go.

sentences.zh: 或問其故，惲曰：「力小任大，剝眾利己，未聞能全者。

translations.literal: When someone asked why, Yun said: "Small strength with a great charge, stripping the masses to enrich oneself—I have never heard that such a man can come through whole.
translations.idiomatic: When someone asked why, Yun said, "Too little strength for too great a charge, stripping the people to enrich oneself—I have never heard of anyone who came through that whole.

sentences.zh: 遠之尚恐見浼，況可近乎！

translations.literal: To keep one's distance from such a man one still fears being tainted—how much less draw near!
translations.idiomatic: Keeping one's distance from such a man one still fears being stained—how much less draw near!

sentences.zh: 」既而果敗，眾服其識。

translations.literal: " Before long Shirong indeed fell; the masses admired Yun's foresight.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Shirong did indeed fall, and everyone admired Yun's judgment.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，授少中大夫、福建閩海道提刑按察使。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he was appointed Gentleman for Grand Attendance and surveillance commissioner of the Fujian-Minhai Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year he was appointed Gentleman for Grand Attendance and surveillance commissioner of the Fujian-Minhai Circuit.

sentences.zh: 黜官吏貪污不法者凡數十人；

translations.literal: He removed several score officials guilty of corruption and lawlessness;
translations.idiomatic: He dismissed several dozen corrupt and lawless officials;

sentences.zh: 察系囚之冤滯者，決而遣之；

translations.literal: he examined prisoners wrongly detained, decided their cases, and sent them away;
translations.idiomatic: he reviewed prisoners wrongly held, decided their cases, and released them;

sentences.zh: 戒戍兵無得寓民家，而創營屋以居之。

translations.literal: he forbade garrison troops to lodge in private homes and had barracks built for them to live in.
translations.idiomatic: he forbade garrison troops to lodge in private homes and had barracks built for them.

sentences.zh: 每謂為治之本在於得人，乃進言於朝曰：「福建所轄郡縣五十餘，連山距海，實為邊徼重地。

translations.literal: He often said the foundation of governance lies in getting the right men, and memorialized to the court: "The fifty-odd commanderies and counties under Fujian lie among mountains and face the sea; they are truly a vital border region.
translations.idiomatic: He often said that the foundation of good government lies in getting the right men, and memorialized to the court, "The more than fifty commanderies and counties under Fujian stretch among mountains to the sea and are truly a vital frontier region.

sentences.zh: 而民情輕詭，由平定以來官吏貪殘，故山寇往往嘯聚，愚民因而蟻附，剽掠村落，官兵致討，复蹂踐之甚，非朝廷一視同仁之意也。

translations.literal: Yet the people's hearts are lightly deceitful; since pacification officials have often been greedy and cruel, mountain bandits frequently gather and shout; foolish commoners then cling to them like ants; they plunder villages, and when government troops come to punish them they again trample the people worse—this is not what the court intends in treating all with equal kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the people are lightly deceitful. Since pacification, officials have often been greedy and cruel, so mountain bandits frequently gather; foolish commoners swarm to join them and plunder villages, and when government troops come to suppress them they trample the people all the worse. This is not what the court intends in treating all with equal kindness.

sentences.zh: 今雖不能一一擇任守令，而行省官僚如平章、左丞尚缺，宜特選清望素著、簡在帝心、文足以撫綏黎庶、武足以折衝外侮者，使鎮靜之，庶幾治安可期矣。

translations.literal: Though we cannot now choose every prefect and magistrate one by one, among the branch secretariat officials such as pacification commissioner and left vice directorship posts still stand vacant. Worthies of clear reputation long established, specially noted in the Emperor's heart, whose learning suffices to soothe the people and whose martial capacity suffices to repel external aggression, should be chosen to pacify the region—then order may perhaps be expected.
translations.idiomatic: Though we cannot now choose every prefect and magistrate individually, posts such as pacification commissioner and left vice director in the branch secretariat still stand vacant. Men of clear reputation long established, specially favored by the Emperor, whose civil capacity suffices to soothe the people and whose martial capacity suffices to repel outside aggression, should be chosen to pacify the region—then order may perhaps be expected.

sentences.zh: 」時行省討劇賊鐘明亮無功，惲复條陳列利害曰：「福建歸附之民戶幾百萬，黃華一變，十去四五。

translations.literal: " At the time the branch secretariat's campaign against the major bandit Zhong Mingliang had failed; Yun again submitted a detailed statement of advantages and dangers: "The submitted households of Fujian number nearly millions; at Huang Hua's rebellion four or five tenths were lost.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the branch secretariat's campaign against the major bandit Zhong Mingliang had failed. Yun again submitted a detailed statement of advantages and dangers: "The submitted households of Fujian number nearly in the millions. At Huang Hua's rebellion four or five tenths were lost.

sentences.zh: 今劇賊猖獗，又酷於華，其可以尋常草竊視之？

translations.literal: Now the major bandit rages fiercely, more savage than Hua—can he be regarded as an ordinary petty outlaw?
translations.idiomatic: Now this major bandit rages fiercely, more savage than Hua—can he be treated as an ordinary petty outlaw?

sentences.zh: 況其地有溪山之險，東擊西走，出沒難測，招之不降，攻之不克，宜選精兵，申明號令，專命重臣節制，以計討之，使彼勢窮力竭，庶可取也。」

translations.literal: Moreover the terrain offers the peril of streams and mountains; striking east and fleeing west, he appears and vanishes unpredictably. If summoning him does not bring surrender and attacking him does not overcome him, fine troops should be chosen, orders clearly proclaimed, and a high minister specially entrusted with overall command to take him by strategy, until his strength is exhausted and his power spent—then he may perhaps be taken."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the terrain offers the peril of streams and mountains; he strikes east and flees west, appearing and vanishing unpredictably. Summoning him does not bring surrender and attacking him does not overcome him. Fine troops should be chosen, orders clearly proclaimed, and a high minister specially entrusted with overall command to take him by strategy until his strength is exhausted and his power spent—then he may perhaps be taken."
